articles.title: Crypto Today: Metaplanet US Expansion, USD1 Decline, Qubic Hack
articles.text:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, Metaplanet secured shareholder approval to take a 93.7% stake in Nasdaq-listed Super League as part of its US expansion, World Liberty Financial’s USD1 stablecoin lost more than $400 million in market capitalization over two weeks and layer-1 blockchain Qubic halted its network after an attacker stole roughly $1.4 million from more than 1,400 wallets.
Metaplanet gains shareholder approval for US Bitcoin treasury expansion
Shareholders of Nasdaq-listed Super League have approved a transaction that would give Japanese Bitcoin treasury company Metaplanet a 93.7% ownership stake in exchange for 2,100 BTC and $2.5 million in cash.
Under the agreement, Metaplanet will receive nearly 45 million common shares, preferred stock carrying governance rights and warrants to purchase additional shares. The deal would give Metaplanet control of Super League’s board and major corporate decisions.
Super League plans to rebrand as Superplanet and trade under the ticker SUPA, shifting its business toward accumulating Bitcoin. The company intends to fund future purchases primarily through preferred stock offerings rather than conventional debt.
The transaction would also give Metaplanet access to US dollar-denominated capital markets, supplementing its existing fundraising activities in Japan. Metaplanet could invest an additional $210 million through junior preferred shares.
Metaplanet currently holds 44,000 BTC, making it the second-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder behind Strategy. The company has also proposed allocating up to 15% of its assets to strategic investments aimed at supporting Bitcoin purchases and dividend payments.
World Liberty’s USD1 stablecoin sheds $400M in market cap
World Liberty Financial’s USD1 stablecoin has shed over $400 million in market capitalization over the past two weeks, driven by large redemptions on Ethereum and BNB Chain.
On Monday, CoinGecko data showed USD1’s market capitalization at about $4.02 billion, down from $4.43 billion on Oct. 6. That’s a decline of approximately $401 million, or 9.1%. World Liberty Financial’s proof-of-reserves dashboard separately showed approximately $4.01 billion in reserves.
The decline extends a period of concentrated redemptions on Ethereum and BNB Chain, according to blockchain research firm Onchain Benchmark. The research platform found that nearly $200 million in BNB Chain redemptions originated from a single unidentified address, although it could not establish who controlled the funds or why they were redeemed.
Despite the redemptions, USD1 maintained its dollar peg throughout the period examined by Onchain Benchmark, trading between $0.998 and $1.000.
The researchers found no evidence of a sustained depegging event, indicating that the decline in circulating supply was not accompanied by a significant loss of the token’s dollar value.
Qubic freezes chain after attacker drains 1.4K wallets with weak seeds
Layer-1 blockchain network Qubic halted operations Sunday after an attacker reportedly exploited weakly generated wallet seeds to drain approximately $1.4 million from more than 1,400 accounts, according to the project.
In a statement on X, Qubic said the network was halted at tick 85,371,949, where it remains paused at the time of writing. Qubic said the vulnerability affected wallet seeds generated using any browser on an iPhone or iPad, Safari on a Mac until Oct. 18, 2026, or the Qubic iOS app before July 2025, leading to 2.94 trillion Qubit (QU) stolen.
“87.1% of the drained funds never left the Qubic network and remain frozen in place,” said Qubic. “The remaining 12.9% was sent to MEXC, whose team froze the receiving account within about an hour.”
The Qubic theft is the latest in a series of attacks tied to weak wallet seeds. In July, Coldcard disclosed that attackers had stolen funds from wallets whose seeds were weakened by a firmware bug. Similar flaws affected Trust Wallet’s browser extension and the Libbitcoin Explorer tool in 2023.

articles.title: SEC to Move Forward With Proposed Crypto Rules After Failed CLARITY Vote
articles.text:
Market participants weigh in on SEC’s proposed crypto regulations
The financial agency is scheduled to close public comments on its ‘Regulation Crypto Assets’ proposed in August.
The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is set to move forward with digital asset policies after Congress failed to pass legislation that would have established a framework for regulating cryptocurrency at the agency and across other parts of government.
On Tuesday, the SEC will close to public comments on its ‘Regulation Crypto Assets,’ a set of rules proposed in August intended to create what the agency called a “clear and fit-for-purpose framework for certain investment contracts involving crypto assets.” Over the 60-day period, the agency gathered about 140 comments from interest groups and individuals on rules and regulations related to a proposed safe harbor that would prevent token issuers from being considered “investment contracts,” as well as exemptions for companies permitting offerings up to a certain amount.
The Markets in Crypto Assets (MiCA) Crypto Alliance, a group established to help organizations looking to implement the EU framework on digital assets, largely supported the SEC’s proposed changes to disclosure requirements. The alliance recommended specific amendments to have the SEC better define “concepts and data structures specific to crypto assets and the disclosure requirements.”
Others, including SkyBridge Capital founder Anthony Scaramucci, said they would support the SEC’s proposed crypto rules. Scaramucci said the digital asset regulations responded to “organic adoption” and “represent a return to the Commission’s proper role” without citing inaction from Congress on the Digital Asset Market Clarity (CLARITY) Act. Six people submitted comments anonymously.
While many public comments praised the SEC’s efforts to advance crypto regulation or said they would be open to further discussion, some legal experts suggest the rules could be more easily overturned than an act of Congress. Both financial agencies overseeing aspects of the crypto industry, the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, are also still understaffed at the leadership level.
Related: House Finance panel chair says regulator actions on crypto ‘fall short’ of CLARITY bill

articles.title: Visa and Mesh Team Up to Expand Crypto and Stablecoin Payments
articles.text:
Visa, Mesh partner to enable crypto spending at 175M merchant locations
Mesh will connect crypto and stablecoin wallets to Visa’s global payment network, allowing users to spend digital assets without a separate card.
Visa and crypto payments network Mesh have partnered to allow consumers to spend cryptocurrency and stablecoin balances directly from digital wallets at merchants across Visa’s global payment network.
The integration will allow users of participating wallets to pay in stores or online without transferring funds to a bank account or obtaining a separate crypto card, according to a Monday announcement from Mesh. Merchants will receive payments through Visa’s existing network without changing their checkout systems.
Visa’s network covers more than 175 million merchant locations across over 200 countries and territories. Mesh said participating wallets, supported devices and launch dates will be announced as rollout plans are finalized.
Mesh will handle transaction funding and conversion between cryptocurrencies, stablecoins and fiat currencies, with Visa payment credentials provisioned through participating wallet apps. The company will also manage customer onboarding and Know Your Customer (KYC) requirements.
The partnership follows Mesh’s integration with Bybit Pay in September, allowing users to spend directly from their exchange balances on supported platforms. In January, Mesh raised $75 million in a Dragonfly-led funding round that valued the company at $1 billion.

articles.title: Mastercard Launches Stablecoin Risk Screening Tool for Banks
articles.text:
Mastercard launches stablecoin risk screening for banks and payment providers
The new service combines payment data and blockchain analytics to help banks detect suspicious stablecoin transactions before settlement.
Mastercard is extending its payment risk controls to stablecoin transactions by introducing a tool that lets financial institutions flag suspicious activity before funds move onchain, where recovering stolen funds can be difficult.
Unveiled Monday at the Money20/20 USA conference, Mastercard’s Stablecoin Security combines traditional payment data with blockchain analytics to identify fraud, scams, sanctions exposure and other financial crime risks. Borderless.xyz and Keyrails are the initial partners, with global commercial availability expected next year.
Banks already use fraud detection to monitor conventional payments. Stablecoins add complexity because funds can move across multiple wallets and blockchains, making it harder to assess risk throughout a transaction. Mastercard said Stablecoin Security can generate a risk score before a payment is completed, allowing banks to identify transactions that may require further review.
The launch marks another expansion of Mastercard’s stablecoin business following its $1.8 billion acquisition of BVNK in August. It also follows the company’s recent announcement of a Global Money Platform designed to bring stablecoin payments to businesses.
Mastercard’s stablecoin expansion comes as growth in the supply of digital dollars has slowed significantly this year, even as transaction volumes have accelerated, driven in part by remittances and cross-border payments. A recent Standard Chartered report suggests the stablecoin market could reach $2 trillion by 2030, two years later than its initial forecast.
Related: Mastercard, Borderless test shared identity checks for stablecoin transfers

articles.title: Revolut Eyes New Crypto Markets After Gibraltar License Approval
articles.text:
Revolut secures Gibraltar crypto license to support global expansion
The UK-based fintech will use the authorization to offer crypto services in additional international markets, though it has not disclosed specific countries or launch dates.
Revolut, a UK-based financial technology company and neobank, has received a cryptocurrency services license in Gibraltar, which it plans to use to expand its digital asset offerings into international markets beyond the UK and European Economic Area.
The Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) granted a Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) Provider license to Revolut Global Digital Assets Limited, a newly established subsidiary, according to a Monday announcement.
A Revolut spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the license will allow the company to offer crypto services in additional international markets, although specific countries and launch timelines have not been announced.
Revolut currently provides cryptocurrency services through Revolut Ltd in the UK and Revolut Digital Assets Europe Ltd across the European Economic Area, where its operations fall under the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).
The fintech reports more than 80 million retail customers worldwide, including about 16 million cryptocurrency users, according to its announcement.
The Gibraltar license follows Revolut’s in-principle approval to offer crypto services in Dubai in July and preliminary conditional approval from US regulators in September to establish a national bank offering digital asset custody and crypto-related payment services.

articles.title: Strive Buys $335 Million in Bitcoin After Investors Pour In $369 Million - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Strive bought 4,045 BTC between October 12 and 16 at about $82,803 each, raising its holdings to 36,818 BTC.
- Warrant exercises on October 12 and 13 raised about $369.2 million and added 13,674,703 Class A shares, and no traditional warrants remain.
- Strive priced a $630 million offering of 15% SATS preferred stock on October 15, set to settle October 20.
Strive, a Nasdaq-listed company that holds Bitcoin as a treasury asset, bought 4,045 BTC between October 12 and 16, according to a regulatory filing published Monday.
The average price was about $82,803 per coin, meaning the stash was worth about $335 million, and the purchase lifts its holdings to 36,818 BTC, up from 32,773 a week earlier. That’s a total just north of $3 billion worth of Bitcoin at today’s prices.
The money comes from a Wall Street machine that has become a steady source of Bitcoin buying: public companies sell shares to investors, then put the cash into Bitcoin. Their stock gives investors exposure to Bitcoin’s price through an ordinary brokerage account.
This week’s cash came from warrants, contracts that let holders buy new shares at a fixed price. On October 12 and 13, investors exercised 273,493,909 of them for 13,674,703 new Class A shares, raising about $369.2 million. The leftovers expired unexercised on October 13, and the filing says no traditional warrants remain.
Class A shares outstanding rose from 101.2 million to 114.8 million in a week, about 13.5%. That shrinks each existing shareholder’s slice of the company unless the new cash earns it back. Strive ended the week with $317.5 million in cash, up $7.2 million.
Strive began in 2022 as an anti-ESG asset manager co-founded by former presidential candidate Vivek Ramaswamy. It adopted Bitcoin as a treasury reserve in May 2025 as it moved to merge with a listed company called Asset Entities, then agreed that September to buy Semler Scientific, a medical device maker holding about 5,000 BTC, in an all-stock deal valued at about $1.3 billion.
When Semler shareholders approved the deal in January, the combined company held roughly 12,800 BTC, so holdings are up almost 3X since. Strive’s previous purchase was 3,311 BTC, about $280 million, at roughly $84,500 per coin, a week before this one. The last 1,223 coins in this week’s batch, bought October 14 to 16, averaged about $81,734.
Strategy, the largest corporate bitcoin holder, also bought last week: 267 BTC for about $22.1 million at roughly $82,900 each, bringing its total to 848,517 BTC. It also spent $193.1 million repurchasing its own STRC preferred stock, a security of which Strive holds 505,000 shares, and it increased its preferred-stock buyback program from $2 billion to $3 billion.
MSCI, the index provider whose benchmarks many funds are built to track, finalized a rule on October 15 targeting “non-operating companies.” Companies that fail a screen for substantial operating assets and a follow-up financial test would be dropped from its indexes as of the close of November 30.
Strategy’s Michael Saylor had called the proposal discriminatory in a September letter, and MSCI will publish the final list of affected companies on November 11.
Across the digital asset treasury space, Tom Lee’s Bitmine added 12,535 ETH, about $30 million, and now holds 6,041,481 ETH, or 4.9% of Ethereum’s roughly 122.1 million tokens. Lee has said buying will stop once the firm hits 5%, and he cited a broad risk-off shift (investors pulling back from risky assets), AI funding worries, U.S.-Iran tensions, midterm election jitters, and rising bond yields.
Strive meanwhile priced an upsized offering on October 15 of 7 million shares of a new 15% Series A Perpetual preferred stock, called SATS, at $90 each, for expected gross proceeds of about $630 million.
Preferred stock pays a set dividend when the board declares it, similar to a bond’s interest but not guaranteed, and “perpetual” means it has no maturity date. The dividend here is 15% of the $100 stated amount, or $15 a year, about 16.7% for buyers paying $90.
The dividends are cumulative, meaning any that go unpaid keep accruing. Strive plans to park $22.50 per share in a reserve for the first 18 months of dividends. The offering is scheduled to settle on October 20, and regular dividend dates start November 9.

articles.title: Metaplanet to Acquire 93.7% of Super League in Bitcoin Deal
articles.text:
Metaplanet to take 93.7% stake in Super League through 2,100 BTC deal
The transaction would give Metaplanet access to US capital markets, where it plans to use preferred stock offerings to finance additional Bitcoin purchases.
Shareholders of Super League, a Nasdaq-listed gaming and digital media company, approved a deal that would give Japanese Bitcoin treasury firm Metaplanet a 93.7% ownership stake, paving the way for its expansion into US capital markets through a publicly traded Bitcoin treasury company.
According to a Monday announcement and filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), shareholders approved the issuance of as many as 435.9 million common shares under agreements involving Metaplanet and Evo Fund. Metaplanet will contribute 2,100 Bitcoin (BTC) and $2.5 million in cash in exchange for 44.86 million common shares, 100 shares of convertible perpetual preferred stock carrying governance rights and 10-year warrants for additional common stock.
The transaction would give Metaplanet control over the company, including the ability to designate a majority of its board and approve major corporate decisions. Metaplanet’s common shares will be subject to a five-year lock-up.
As part of the deal, Super League plans to rebrand as Superplanet and adopt the Nasdaq ticker SUPA, with a strategy focused on increasing its Bitcoin holdings per share.
Rather than relying primarily on debt, Superplanet intends to finance additional Bitcoin purchases through senior, non-convertible perpetual preferred shares. Metaplanet will also have the option to invest up to $210 million in junior preferred stock to provide additional financial support.
Source: Dylan LeClair, Metaplanet director of Bitcoin strategy
The deal comes as Metaplanet continues to expand its Bitcoin holdings. The company has accumulated 44,000 BTC, making it the second-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder behind Strategy, according to industry data.
Related: Metaplanet to issue $329M convertible bonds to pay debt, fund share buybacks
Metaplanet looks to US markets to finance Bitcoin purchases
The deal would enable Metaplanet to raise capital in US dollars through preferred stock offerings, complementing its existing yen-denominated financing in Japan.
In an Oct. 15 SEC filing, Super League said the US market for preferred securities issued by Bitcoin treasury companies has grown large enough to support new entrants. The proposed financing structure would provide another source of funding for Bitcoin purchases without relying primarily on conventional debt.
The expansion comes as Metaplanet revises its broader investment strategy. Earlier this month, the company proposed allocating up to 15% of its total assets for strategic investments to help finance Bitcoin purchases and dividend payments.
Related: Metaplanet CEO shuts down Bitcoin sale speculation after $322M transfer

articles.title: Strive Buys $335M in Bitcoin, Holdings Reach 36,818 BTC
articles.text:
Strive buys $335M in Bitcoin, boosting holdings to 36,818 BTC
The Bitcoin treasury company added another 1,223 BTC after an earlier purchase pushed it past MARA Holdings, while continuing to expand its reserves through equity financing.
Bitcoin treasury company Strive purchased 4,045 Bitcoin for approximately $335 million last week, bringing its total holdings to 36,818 BTC as it continues to expand its cryptocurrency reserves through equity financing.
The company acquired the Bitcoin (BTC) between Oct. 12-16 at an average price of $82,803 per coin, including fees and expenses, according to a Monday filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.
Strive is now the fourth-largest publicly traded corporate BTC holder, ahead of MARA Holdings, with reserves valued at approximately $3 billion, according to data from BitcoinTreasuries.net. MARA was reported to be selling some of its holdings, as Arkham tracked wallets linked to the miner depositing about $82 million worth of the crypto into Binance and Gate in recent days.
Strive’s Bitcoin holdings reached 36,818 BTC. Source: BitcoinTreasuries.NET
Strive also reported approximately $369 million in proceeds from warrant exercises on Oct. 12 and 13, resulting in the issuance of 13.7 million common shares. Its effective share count rose 12.4%, roughly matching the 12.3% increase in Bitcoin holdings and leaving BTC per share largely unchanged.
The latest acquisition follows a series of large Bitcoin purchases by the company, including a 3,311 purchase the previous week, when its holdings grew 11.2%, outpacing a 9.4% increase in its effective common share count.
Strive also announced the launch of SATS last week, a new preferred stock issue carrying a fixed 15% annual dividend, payable each business day beginning Nov. 9, subject to board approval. The company priced a $630 million offering of the new preferred shares last week, with proceeds potentially funding additional Bitcoin purchases.
Strive (ASST) shares were up around 7.7% at $25.95 in late-morning trading Monday, according to Yahoo Finance data.

articles.title: Anthropic Gives 5% of Itself to the Public. Musk Answers by Giving Away SpaceX Shares - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Anthropic will commit 5% of its shares to a new Public Benefit Fund, subject to stockholder approval, and says roughly 20% of its stock will go to public causes once co-founder and employee pledges are counted.
- Elon Musk responded by promising one SpaceX share to every child in the United States next year, a giveaway worth more than $10 billion at current prices.
- The fund follows a draft AI safety bill Anthropic pitched to lawmakers days earlier, which would let the government block models that risk killing or injuring more than 50 people or causing over $1 billion in damage.
Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, said Sunday it will commit 5% of its shares to a new Public Benefit Fund. On Monday, Elon Musk answered by promising one SpaceX share to every child in the United States next year.
“The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will have increased flexibility and scale, enabling us to pursue our mission in new ways: for example, we might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations,” Anthropic said. The company has already committed $200 million to studying that.
Americans are uneasy about how fast AI is moving: an AP-NORC poll in late September found that 64% of U.S. adults say the technology is developing too fast, and 8% say too slow.
Anthropic is preparing an IPO, meaning it would sell its shares to the public on the stock market, as soon as November at a reported valuation of around $2 trillion. At that price, 5% of the company would be worth about $100 billion on paper, though that is the value of the shares, not cash sitting in an account.
The fund is set up as a wholly owned LLC rather than a nonprofit, which Anthropic says gives it room to switch between types of giving. The board can add another 2% of shares each time the company's value rises 50% above a baseline that has not been disclosed, and none of the fund's equity can be used for lobbying or political donations.
The co-founders' pledge to donate 80% of their equity and a matching program for employee donations, and Anthropic says roughly 20% of its shares will be dedicated to the public good. The company has not said how the fund will be taxed or what it will disclose publicly, as a traditional charity must.
Musk, never one to leave the spotlight to someone else, pushed for Universal High Income (as opposed to Universal Basic Income) writing on X that he will give one of his SpaceX shares to every kid in America. "This will be the first of many," he added.
His first reply to Anthropic, recommending "giving the shares directly to the public" instead of routing them through a fund, came Sunday night, and the pledge for kids followed early Monday, less than a day after Anthropic's announcement.
Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America.
This will be the first of many.
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 19, 2026
With roughly 72 million children in the country, the pledge comes to about $10.5 billion at SpaceX's price of roughly $147 a share. That is just over 1% of the 6.42 billion shares Musk held as of June 30, per an SEC filing, and about the same slice of a fortune estimated at $908.5 billion that has crossed $1 trillion several times this year.
The Treasury Department recently let companies and charities donate individual company shares to Trump Accounts, tax-advantaged savings accounts for children, with donated stock generally held for five years. This is likely the option Musk is going for instead of Anthropic’s path of creating a fund, which he more or less confirmed in a reply post on X.
Thanks for helping enable this
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 19, 2026
The Anthropic giveaway comes from a company whose CEO wrote in January that "we are considerably closer to real danger in 2026" and which is known to preach the gospel of AI doomerism while maxing out accelerationism, releasing the most powerful AI models on the market.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman accused Anthropic in April of using fear-based marketing to promote Claude Mythos, and Anthropic is now giving away a slice of itself ahead of a stock market debut.
Two days before the fund, Anthropic had quietly presented lawmakers with its own draft AI safety bill. It would let the government block the release of a model posing a foreseeable, imminent risk of killing or seriously injuring more than 50 people or causing over $1 billion in damage, through a bioweapon, an AI slipping beyond human control, or a cyberattack.
A block would have to run through the Commerce Department and a federal court order, and developers would publish safety frameworks and transparency reports for new models. Anthropic says the bill reflects its Advanced AI Framework, promoted to lawmakers since June, the month CEO Dario Amodei called for binding rules on frontier models, meaning the most powerful AI systems.
Anthropic critics include investor and former White House AI czar David Sacks, who responded to the company’s pledge with his own post on X: “You’ve put 20% of your equity in an LCC. Whether it serves the public good remains to be seen.”
Anthropic says it will release the fund's governance structure and valuation thresholds in the coming months, and its IPO could come as early as November.

articles.title: XRP Ledger Repairs Its Lending Protocol Before It Goes Live - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- XRP Ledger developers are patching its new lending protocol before it goes live, adding a follow-up amendment to fix the original LendingProtocol code while it’s still in the network’s voting queue.
- The protocol enables on-chain, fixed-term, uncollateralized loans using pooled funds and “first-loss capital” to absorb defaults, relying on off-chain underwriting rather than automated collateral; amendments need 80% validator support over two weeks to activate.
- The pre-launch fix follows a recent near-miss when developers patched a dormant payment-engine bug that could have minted counterfeit XRP.
The XRP Ledger is patching its new lending feature before a single loan has been written on it, adding a second code amendment to repair the system while it waits in the network’s approval queue.
The ledger’s lending protocol, a DeFi building block that enables on-chain, fixed-term, uncollateralized loans drawn from pooled funds, was introduced through an amendment called LendingProtocol that is still open for validator voting.
Rather than wait for that version to go live and then fix it, developers have published a follow-up, LendingProtocolV1_1, that corrects issues in the original before it ever takes effect. The documentation now lists both amendments as requirements for the feature, meaning the network would adopt the repaired version from the start.
The approach reflects how changes reach the XRP Ledger. New features and fixes ship as amendments that must earn support from at least 80% of trusted validators over a two-week period before activating.
Because the original lending code hasn’t cleared that bar yet, patching it with a second amendment avoids launching a known-flawed system onto the live network, then scrambling to repair it afterward.
The protocol itself is built for institutional-style credit rather than the collateral-and-liquidation model common in DeFi. It relies on off-chain underwriting to vet borrowers and uses “first-loss capital,” a buffer a loan broker puts up to absorb the initial hit from defaults, in place of automated on-chain collateral. Issuers retain compliance tools, including the ability to freeze accounts or claw back funds.
The caution follows a close call elsewhere in the ledger’s code. Developers recently disclosed and fixed a critical bug in the XRP Ledger’s payment engine that could have let an attacker mint counterfeit XRP, a flaw that sat dormant for roughly a decade before a researcher flagged it. Fixing the lending code pre-launch fits a more cautious posture around new functionality.
The lending feature is part of a broader buildout of credit and DeFi capabilities on the XRP Ledger, which has been adding the financial-market plumbing Ripple and others have long said it lacked.

articles.title: Bitcoin Asks Above $83,000 Limit BTC Price Upside as US Stocks Rebound
articles.text:
Bitcoin is rejected at $83K as US bond yields reverse higher with equities
Bitcoin price action failed to improve with equities as a sell wall at $83,000 kept BTC in a tight range.
Bitcoin (BTC) traded below $82,000 after Monday’s Wall Street open as crypto diverged from rising stocks and bond yields.
Key points:
- Bitcoin gave up early-week gains as ask liquidity amassed above $83,000 across exchanges.
- The Nasdaq Composite Index followed Asian equities higher, gaining 1.5% in the first hours of trading on Monday.
- US bond yields continued to move in lockstep with stocks, with the 10-year yield back at 5.13% ahead of major corporate earnings announcements.
Bitcoin treads water as stocks, bond yields rebound
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD dipping to $81,678 on Bitstamp after reaching $83,062 earlier in the day.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Both Asia and US equities rallied to start the week, helping to recoup losses from the week prior as selling pressure on tech stocks eased. South Korea’s tech-heavy KOSPI Composite Index finished the day 1.76% higher at 5,768 points, while the Nasdaq Composite Index was up 1.5% at the time of writing.
Nasdaq Composite Index one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Continuing a pattern observed in recent weeks, US bond yields rose in lockstep with equities ahead of anticipated strong corporate earnings by tech giants. Several of these are due for release on Tuesday and Wednesday, including Meta, SpaceX and Tesla. The US 10-year and 30-year yields reached 5.13% and 5.46%, respectively.
US 10-year bond yield one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
In its latest analysis, trading company QCP Capital saw bond-market stability as key to Bitcoin upside momentum. It also warned that BTC could suffer from a repeat of last week’s tech-stock sell-off.
“Broader equity deleveraging dynamics could transmit to cryptocurrency markets and potentially threaten the $80,000 support level if sustained. Conversely, a sustained Treasury rally could provide support for risk assets, particularly if accompanied by declining real yields and a weaker US dollar,” it wrote.
$83,000 sellers keep BTC price in check
On lower time frames, Bitcoin price action encountered friction after ask liquidity thickened above $83,000 on exchange order books.
Related: Stocks rebound into key tech earnings: Three things to know in Bitcoin this week
Data from CoinGlass showed this wall of asks pressuring BTC/USD lower, while 24-hour cross-crypto liquidations totaled $335 million.
Crypto liquidation heatmap. Source: CoinGlass
Amid rangebound conditions, onchain analytics platform CryptoQuant showed Bitcoin whales reducing activity. The Binance whale ratio, which records the share of the 10 largest inflow transactions relative to total inflows, fell to 0.45 from 0.54 at the start of October.
“The decline in the Whale Ratio indicates that the proportion of large BTC deposit transactions relative to total exchange inflows is decreasing, potentially reflecting shifts in whales’ trading strategies and asset management activities,” CryptoQuant summarized.
Binance Bitcoin exchange whale ratio. Source: CryptoQuant

articles.title: Made An ‘Honest’ Mistake With Crypto Taxes? New Bill Offers Way Out
articles.text:
Made an ‘honest’ mistake with crypto taxes? New bill offers way out
A proposed US bill would let crypto investors correct past tax reporting mistakes through a dedicated disclosure program, with reduced penalties for eligible taxpayers.
Crypto investors who failed to report trades in previous years may soon breathe a sigh of relief thanks to legislation currently advancing in the US Congress.
Section 502 of the Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act, H.R. 10357, would require the Treasury secretary to establish a Digital Asset Voluntary Disclosure Program within 12 months of the bill becoming law.
That would allow eligible taxpayers to correct any past digital asset tax violation by filing amended returns and paying the tax owed, along with interest and a program penalty.
The House Ways and Means Committee approved the bill by a 38-5 vote on Sept. 16, but it has not become law yet; it still has to pass the House and Senate and be signed by the president.
“It’s a big change that would help a lot of ordinary taxpayers, and it has gotten very little attention,” Andrew Gordon, executive director of Digital Asset Tax Action, tells Magazine.
A gap in the system
Crypto investors in the US are already grappling with the first filing season under the new 1099-DA broker reporting rules, which give the IRS greater visibility into crypto transactions.
Gordon says those rules should make reporting easier going forward, but they fail to address the years before coming into effect.
The House Ways and Means Committee approved the bill by a 38-5 vote. Source: Ways & Means
“A large share of investors didn’t report correctly over the years,” he says, and existing procedures don’t offer taxpayers who made “honest mistakes” a predictable way to resolve their liabilities.
Related: Greece plans 10% capital gains tax on cryptocurrencies
“Today, a crypto investor who learns they didn’t properly report their crypto or has not reported at all has no good way to fix it,” he says; investors can discover years later that they misunderstood the tax treatment of crypto-to-crypto trades or reporting activity across multiple platforms.
What taxpayers could get
The IRS’s existing Voluntary Disclosure Practice is aimed at taxpayers who willfully violated tax rules and face potential criminal exposure.
For taxpayers with errant reporting skills, they can currently correct their mistakes by filing amended returns, but the penalty treatment is not as predictable as provision 502’s proposed crypto-specific program.
Sharon Yip, a certified public accountant (CPA) and founder of Crypto Tax Advisors, says reporting errors among ordinary crypto investors are common.
In her firm’s experience, some clients did not report crypto because they believed no tax was due until they cashed out, while others relied on incomplete exchange records or incorrectly classified transactions.
“There is no standardized process that gives non-willful crypto investors predictable penalty treatment or a clear resolution,” Yip tells Magazine.
She says a crypto-specific program could “fill this gap” by providing a “defined correction period, reduced and predictable penalties and greater certainty for taxpayers who come forward voluntarily.”
What the bill would offer
Under Section 502, taxpayers would generally have to file amended returns within 24 months of the program being established, and the bill sets out two penalty tracks.
There are lower rates for taxpayers who certify under penalty of perjury that their violations were neither fraudulent nor willful. They would face a 0% penalty on the first $25,000 of tax deficiency per year and 5% on amounts above that, if they file within the first 12 months of the program.
For those who don’t certify, rates of 25% on the first $25,000 and 40% above it apply, with the rates increasing if taxpayers miss the initial window.
49% of crypto users understood selling crypto can be a taxable event. Source: Cointracker
There is also relief from specified civil penalties, and taxpayers who don’t certify are protected from criminal referrals based on information properly disclosed for the tax offenses covered by the provision.
Yip says taxpayers should check their transaction histories across exchanges and wallets to identify which years need correcting before assessing whether their mistakes were genuinely non-willful.
Because falsely certifying carries a penalty of perjury, she advises seeking professional guidance where taxpayers are unsure.
Section 502 could come as a welcome relief for many US crypto users; a 2026 report by CoinTracker and Coinbase found that only 49% correctly understood that selling crypto can be a taxable event.

articles.title: Hackers Are Running Apple's iOS on Android Phones for the First Time - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Videos of iOS 16 booting on a Redmi Note 12 and a Nothing 3a spread on X, with the Redmi Note 12 clip posted October 18 passing 2 million views.
- The open-source ios-sweet project pairs Apple's XNU kernel with unmodified iOS 16.7.16 files on a Snapdragon 732G phone, but Wi-Fi, mobile data, audio, camera and graphics acceleration do not work yet.
- Android first ran on iPhones through iDroid in April 2010, and Corellium's Project Sandcastle repeated the feat on newer iPhones about a decade later.
Hobbyists are booting Apple’s iOS, the software that runs iPhones, on Android phones just to prove that they can, and video demonstrations are going viral on social media.
One clip of iOS 16 on a Redmi Note 12 has passed 2 million views on X, and another developer posted a build running on a Nothing 3a.
iOS, the operating system that runs everything on an iPhone from the touchscreen to the apps, is built to run only on Apple’s own hardware. Choosing a phone has meant choosing its software, and the reverse. If that wall cracks, cheap and old phones could one day run software they were never sold with.
Android has run on iPhones before: a project called iDroid let early iPhones boot it in April 2010. A decade later, security firm Corellium launched Project Sandcastle, which put Android 10 on iPhones with Apple’s A10 chip.
Nobody has been able to make it the other way around—until now.
WTf, Running real iOS on Android hardware.
HackiOS is attempting a full code rewrite to run actual iOS on Android hardware.
They’re in the final polishing stage. 
If it works, the project will be completely free and open no paywalls, no premium tiers. pic.twitter.com/oQywSdi9Y5
— Md Ismail Šojal 🕷️ (@0x0SojalSec) October 16, 2026
Users are achieving good results with a combination of tools. The closest public code is an open-source project on GitHub, the site where developers share code, called ios-sweet, built for the Redmi Note 10 Pro.
It takes XNU, the kernel Apple publishes openly (the core of an operating system, which talks to the chip, memory and storage), and patches it to run on that phone’s Qualcomm Snapdragon 732G chip. Unmodified iOS 16.7.16 files from an iPhone X then sit on top.
The “readme” file from its developers calls the project an “experimental bring-up, not a usable phone OS,” and says the Redmi Note 10 Pro reaches the lock screen, home screen, Control Center and Settings, with touch and the buttons responding. Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile data, audio and the camera do not work, the gesture to leave an app does nothing, and with no graphics driver the processor draws the screen at roughly 20 to 30 frames per second.
A separate group calling itself OOSexGang says its HackiOS project runs iOS 16.5 on a Poco X5 Pro, using a custom UEFI (the firmware that starts a device) and the XNU kernel. The researcher sharing the demo notes there is no public source code or independent verification. In a newer clip, Safari downloads an Android app file from APKMirror and then fails to open it, which, to be fair, is what iOS has always done with Android apps.
iOS 16.5 just Running on an Android phone hardware.
and it can’t open Apk because of iOS,
Safari pulls an APK from APKMirror, then fails to run it.
New HackiOs/OOSexGang demo it can be soon public release https://t.co/Iv3FDwuXyK pic.twitter.com/TGclBWllxp
— Md Ismail Šojal 🕷️ (@0x0SojalSec) October 19, 2026
The idea of running things where they shouldn’t has been gaining enthusiasts with the advent of AI and the ability to ship code—and improve it—extremely fast. Just days ago. the security firm Calif.io jailbroke an iPhone 18 Pro on stage at the Hexacon conference in Paris, and the root access survived a reboot. Jailbreaking removes Apple’s restrictions to give a user deep control of the phone.
Another major tool that sparked the movement is REA, short for Reverse Engineer Anything, a free toolkit that lets AI coding assistants pick software apart, with examples that included a developer’s demo of GTA V running on iOS.
For now, the practical ceiling of a Redmi Note 10 Pro running iOS is looking at the iOS home screen. Wi-Fi, mobile data, and audio don't work, the screen is drawn by the processor at roughly 20 to 30 frames per second, and the first boot takes four to five minutes on the Apple logo.
Anyone tempted to try it should know the install wipes the phone's Android user data, leaves security protections mostly switched off, and that the devs themselves say not to keep anything personal on the device.

articles.title: Listed Companies Object to OKX-ICE’s Tokenized Stock Plan
articles.text:
Public companies object to OKX-ICE’s tokenized stock plan
Nine public companies objected to having their shares offered in tokenized form by OKX and ICE, testing whether platforms can create blockchain-based markets without issuer consent.
Nine listed companies have formally objected to having their shares offered in tokenized form on the proposed tokenized stock platform backed by OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).
The companies included Cerebras Systems, AppLovin, Applied Digital, Rocket Lab, CoreWeave, Verizon Communications, Applied Optoelectronics, Broadcom and UnitedHealth Group, according to a Thursday notice by OKX and ICE.
The notice did not disclose the reason behind the objection. Under the Securities and Exchange Commission’s Sept. 17 innovation exemption announcement, tokenized venues must give issuers written notice and an opportunity to object before listing third-party tokenized stocks.
“Issuers aren’t objecting to the blockchain. They’re objecting to not knowing what happens to their price once it trades there,” Robin Nordnes, CEO of trading validation platform Raiku, told Cointelegraph. “On a public chain, the validator building the block sets the order. Until desks can measure their distance to that point, best execution is a promise, not a number.”
The objections highlight a potential hurdle for tokenized stocks and test whether crypto platforms can create blockchain-based markets for public company shares without issuer cooperation.
Cointelegraph has approached OKX for comment on the ramifications of the objection but had not received a response by the time of publication.
Tokenized stock offerings need more real-world data to address pricing discrepancy concerns
Companies need to see the “upside and a track record of efficient pricing,” Misha Putiatin, co-founder of collateral markets platform Symbiotic, told Cointelegraph, adding that more “real-world data would help everyone assess the benefits and risks.”
He said that additional institutional tokenization initiatives, such as the Depository Trust and Clearing Corporation’s (DTCC) tokenization services, could instill more confidence in tokenized offerings.
Related: Nasdaq-listed Tron sets up $200M ATM share offering to fuel TRX acquisitions
CoinShares’ senior research associate, Luke Nolan, said the objection does not amount to a rejection of tokenization generally, but mostly against being tokenized without consent. He told Cointelegraph:
“This veto also seems to be venue-specific, as in companies being able to say: no, I don’t want them offered on this venue, but I could permit/launch it somewhere else.” 
Nolan said the concerns are valid, adding that market participants have previously taken advantage of specific market mechanics to cause “squeezes” or “short-term swings” in the underlying asset’s price.
Capital moving onchain during the past 30 days. Source: OnchainBenchmark
More than $754 million in capital has moved onchain during the past 30 days, pushing the total across stablecoins and tokenized assets to $320 billion, according to OnchainBenchmark.

articles.title: Mastercard Brings Its Fraud-Fighting Tools to Stablecoin Payments - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Mastercard launched Stablecoin Security, a risk-intelligence tool that lets financial institutions screen stablecoin payments for fraud, scams and sanctions exposure across the transaction lifecycle, generating a risk score before a payment settles.
- Delivered via a platform-agnostic API with partners Borderless.xyz and Keyrails, it addresses a blind spot flagged by a BIS study finding nearly 60% of 2025 stablecoin transfers were complex, multi-step transactions.
- It extends Mastercard’s stablecoin push—from its BVNK-powered Global Money Platform to AI-agent payments—launching first in North America, with global availability in 2027.
Mastercard is extending its fraud-fighting playbook to stablecoins, launching a tool that lets financial institutions scan dollar-pegged token payments for fraud, scams, and sanctions exposure before the money ever moves on-chain.
Unveiled Monday at the Money20/20 conference in Las Vegas, the product, called Stablecoin Security, combines Mastercard’s payment intelligence with blockchain analytics to assess risk across the full life of a transaction, from the moment a payment is initiated through its movement on a public ledger.
The company launched it with two initial program participants, Borderless.xyz and Keyrails, both alumni of its Start Path blockchain accelerator.
The pitch addresses a growing blind spot as stablecoins move into cross-border and business-to-business payments. Mastercard cited a Bank for International Settlements study of 593 million stablecoin transfers in 2025 that found nearly 60% were complex, multi-step transactions rather than simple one-to-one payments, making it harder for institutions to gauge risk across the whole journey.
Delivered through a platform-agnostic API, the tool analyzes signals like where funds originated, exposure to restricted parties and scam indicators, generating a risk score before a payment settles that slots into existing compliance and fraud workflows.
“Stablecoins are creating new possibilities for value exchange, but financial institutions need the right intelligence and controls to participate with confidence,” said Ann Johnson, Mastercard’s executive vice president of security solutions, framing the tool as an extension of the company’s fraud capabilities into digital assets.
The launch is the latest sign of Mastercard weaving stablecoins into its core business. The company recently rolled out a Global Money Platform with BVNK, the stablecoin infrastructure firm it acquired in August, letting businesses hold and move fiat and stablecoins through a single connection.
It has also secured a New York BitLicense covering stablecoins and tokenized deposits, moved to enable AI-agent payments alongside Coinbase and Ripple, and expanded stablecoin settlement to include Circle’s USDC and Ripple’s RLUSD.
Mastercard said Stablecoin Security builds on existing tools like Crypto Credential and Crypto Secure, and that it plans to extend the product’s reach in 2027, including through BVNK. The solution is launching first in North America, with worldwide availability expected next year.

articles.title: Strategy Buys $22M in Bitcoin, Repurchases $193M in STRC
articles.text:
Strategy buys $22M in Bitcoin, repurchases $193M in STRC
Strategy added 267 Bitcoin to its holdings as it bought back 1.94 million STRC shares and boosted its preferred stock buyback program to $3 billion.
Michael Saylor’s Strategy, the world’s largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder, continued buying Bitcoin last week while spending nearly nine times as much repurchasing its preferred stock.
Strategy bought 267 Bitcoin for $22.1 million at an average price of $82,900 between Oct. 12 and Oct. 18, bringing its holdings to 848,517 BTC, according to a Monday filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
The company also repurchased 1.94 million shares of its Stretch (STRC) preferred stock for $193.1 million and increased its digital credit securities buyback authorization to $3 billion from $2 billion.
The latest transactions extend a trend of management spending more on preferred stock repurchases than Bitcoin purchases, even as Saylor expects a return to a Bitcoin bull market.
Strategy’s STRC buybacks continue to outpace Bitcoin purchases
Strategy funded its latest Bitcoin purchase primarily through $22 million in proceeds from selling 140,872 shares of its common stock, MSTR, while using existing cash for the STRC repurchases.
The company has spent $459.2 million repurchasing STRC shares so far in the fourth quarter, more than six times the $72.3 million it spent acquiring 851 Bitcoin over the same period.
Related: Strategy conditionally declares daily dividends as STRC hovers below $100
STRC is a variable-rate preferred stock designed to pay regular dividends. Strategy has previously said it intends to repurchase shares trading below their $100 stated value to help support the stock’s price.
The company reported a $4.83 billion USD Reserve to support preferred stock dividends and debt interest payments, alongside $447.3 million in separate USD Cash holdings.
Saylor sees Bitcoin returning to a bull market
The heavier spending on STRC buybacks comes as Saylor expressed optimism about Bitcoin’s outlook during a discussion at ParaFi Investor Day on Saturday.
“We’re moving back into a bull market,” Saylor said, pointing to Bitcoin’s recovery above its 200-day simple moving average, a widely followed indicator of longer-term price trends.
Saylor identified restrictive trade, foreign and monetary policies as headwinds for BTC, while highlighting growing bank adoption and the tokenization of traditional financial assets as potential drivers.
Ahead of Monday’s Nasdaq open, MSTR shares were trading more than 2.5% higher in premarket activity, according to Yahoo Finance. The shares closed Friday down about 9.6%, at $138.83 apiece. STRC shares also gained around 0.8% in premarket trading to $98.45, after falling 1.8% on Friday.

articles.title: Why Some of America’s Biggest Companies Are Objecting to Tokenized Shares - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Nine issuers have objected to trading of their shares on OKXICE TSV, the planned tokenized stock venue from OKX and NYSE owner ICE, according to an Oct. 15 public notice.
- Nasdaq has said it will opt its own shares out of the SEC’s innovation exemption, citing concerns about real-time pricing and trade reporting.
- The notice says OKXICE isn’t registered with the SEC or subject to Regulation NMS. It doesn’t say whether the objections will keep those stocks off the platform.
Wall Street’s push to put stocks onchain is running into an unexpected obstacle: the companies behind the stocks.
Nine issuers, including Verizon, Broadcom, and UnitedHealth Group, have objected to having their shares offered on OKXICE TSV, according to an Oct. 15 public notice from the venue.
OKXICE TSV is a planned tokenized stock platform from crypto exchange OKX and NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange. The other objecting companies are Cerebras Systems, AppLovin, Applied Digital, Rocket Lab, CoreWeave, and Applied Optoelectronics.
The notice didn’t say why the companies objected or whether the objections will keep their shares off the platform.
Nasdaq is also keeping its distance. The exchange operator, which isn’t among the nine, has said it would opt its own shares out of the SEC’s framework. A spokesperson told The Wall Street Journal that Nasdaq doesn’t want its stock trading on a venue that doesn’t show the best prices in real time or report trades to the consolidated tape. That’s notable given that Nasdaq won SEC approval earlier this year for its own tokenized securities pilot.
The venue is the first major test of the SEC’s innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate. The exemption lets qualifying platforms trade tokenized U.S. stocks without registering as exchanges. OKXICE plans to run around the clock using Uniswap v4 liquidity pools on OKX’s XLayer blockchain, with trades settled in stablecoins such as USDC and USDT.
The tokens are created by a third party, not the companies themselves. That outside “tokenizer” holds actual shares one-for-one through a registered broker-dealer, and token holders are supposed to receive the same dividends and voting rights as regular shareholders, according to the notice.
The notice also lays out what users give up. OKXICE isn’t registered with the SEC, isn’t subject to Regulation NMS rules designed to ensure investors get the best displayed prices, and doesn’t have to provide fair access to all participants. Trading is capped at a small slice of each stock’s normal volume, and administrators can upgrade the venue’s smart contracts without advance notice.
OKX and ICE first teamed up on tokenized securities earlier this year before announcing the 24/7 venue this month. In terms of appetite from traders and investors for tokenized stocks, the International Monetary Fund recently found real demand for tokenized stocks—especially outside of traditional market hours—but warned that the market remains volatile and illiquid.

articles.title: World Liberty USD1 Stablecoin Market Cap Drops $400M
articles.text:
World Liberty’s USD1 stablecoin sheds $400M in market cap in two weeks
World Liberty Financial’s USD1 stablecoin saw its market cap decrease more than $400 million over two weeks of large redemptions on Ethereum and BNB Chain.
World Liberty Financial’s USD1 stablecoin has shed over $400 million in market capitalization over the past two weeks, driven by large redemptions on Ethereum and BNB Chain.
On Monday, CoinGecko data showed USD1’s market capitalization at about $4.02 billion, down from $4.43 billion on Oct. 6. That’s a decline of approximately $401 million, or 9.1%. World Liberty Financial’s proof-of-reserves dashboard separately showed approximately $4.01 billion in reserves.
The decline extends a period of concentrated redemptions on Ethereum and BNB Chain, according to blockchain research firm Onchain Benchmark. The research platform found that nearly $200 million in BNB Chain redemptions originated from a single unidentified address, although they could not establish who controlled the funds or why they were redeemed.
Despite the redemptions, USD1 maintained its dollar peg throughout the period examined by Onchain Benchmark, trading between $0.998 and $1.000. Onchain Benchmark found no evidence of a sustained depegging event, indicating that the decline in circulating supply was not accompanied by a significant loss of the token’s dollar value.
USD1 supply decline outpaces major stablecoins on Ethereum
According to Onchain Benchmark, Ethereum accounted for $184.60 million in net USD1 redemptions across 63 token burns between Oct. 6 and Oct. 15. BNB Chain recorded $200.43 million across 12 burns.
On Ethereum, more than 99% of tokens sent for redemption passed through a wallet labeled BitGo, USD1’s current issuer and custodian, while the BNB Chain transfers from the unidentified address were made in batches of $30 million to $50 million.
Related: France advances stablecoin tax, eyes self-custodial wallets and exit tax proposals
The reductions were not offset by new issuance on Solana, where USD1 supply remained unchanged at about $1.42 billion during the nine days reviewed by Onchain Benchmark.
“The next tests come with the change of issuer. When World Liberty’s trust company opens, it will take on a token whose size depends on the decisions of a few large holders, under a charter whose legal footing is being argued in court,” Onchain Benchmark said. “Whether fresh mints on Solana, or anywhere else, rebuild the total, or October marks the size USD1 carries into its new issuer, is the question the next weeks of supply data will answer.”
Transfers between Ethereum and BNB Chain totaled less than $1 million, according to the report, suggesting the missing supply wasn’t simply shifted between those networks.
USD1’s supply contraction on Ethereum was steeper than that of several other US dollar-denominated stablecoins between Oct. 6 and Oct. 15. USD1 supply on the network fell 11.45%, compared with declines of 4.93% for USDe, 2.18% for USDC and 0.76% for circulating USDT.

articles.title: US Orders Civilian Agencies to Rip DeepSeek Out of Government Systems - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- DHS directed U.S. civilian agencies on Monday to remove DeepSeek products and third-party services built on the model from their IT systems, and barred new purchases.
- The notice says DeepSeek use "may result in the transfer of sensitive data to the PRC" and could produce intelligence on U.S. persons and agencies.
- The Commerce Department, the Navy, New York, Tennessee and Virginia had already restricted DeepSeek; the FCC votes October 29 on barring Chinese labs from testing electronics for U.S. use.
The U.S. Department of Homeland Security ordered civilian government agencies on Monday to remove DeepSeek, China’s best-known AI chatbot, from their computer systems and to stop buying it, along with any outside service built on top of it.
DHS says the models pose “multiple threat vectors,” meaning several separate ways things can go wrong. Using them “may result in the transfer of sensitive data to the PRC”—the People’s Republic of China—if government employees or vendors use them, and could produce “actionable intelligence on U.S. persons and/or government agencies.”
Deepseek is an open source model that can run locally or hosted by any provider, not just China based. For example, Perplexity runs its own servers located in the United States. That said, the developers host a version in servers located in China for those using Deepseek.com’s services.
The ban reaches past DeepSeek’s own app to third-party services developed using it.
A July DHS memo, made public Monday, had already told agencies to monitor traffic flowing in and out of government websites for DeepSeek-related risks. The Commerce Department and the Navy previously banned DeepSeek on government devices, and New York, Tennessee and Virginia have taken similar steps. The Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately comment.
DeepSeek, a Hangzhou-based startup, became a household name on Jan. 27, 2025, when its open-source model, built for under $5 million, knocked Nvidia’s stock down 16% and erased about $600 billion of the chipmaker’s value. U.S. tech as a whole lost an estimated $1 trillion that day, because Deepseek proved to be similarly capable than America’s best models while costing a fraction of the price, with the possibility of running for free on the appropriate infrastructure.
Italy’s data protection authority also ordered DeepSeek to block its chatbot days later, calling the company’s answers to its privacy questions “totally insufficient.” In April 2025, a House select committee on the Chinese Communist Party alleged that DeepSeek secretly sends American user data to the Chinese government..
The same committee said DeepSeek may have used about 60,000 Nvidia chips, including 20,000 restricted under U.S. export controls, the rules that bar selling the most advanced AI chips to China.
DeepSeek has kept shipping since: the preview of its V4-Pro model, released in April, is priced about 98% below OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 Pro and is free to download and modify under an MIT license, and this week it released an updated version of its V4.1-Flash model aimed at efficiency with big quality gains.
The notice lands in the middle of a wider federal push against Chinese technology as the Federal Communications Commission votes on October 29 on barring all Chinese labs from testing electronics for U.S. use.

articles.title: Whale loses $469,000 in hours on Hyperliquid, yet re-enters with $16M ETH short bet
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Hyperliquid forcibly closed 8,162.8 ETH of an unknown wallet's short, realizing about $469,000 in losses before fees.
- The wallet added another 1,126 ETH of shorts that afternoon, bringing its position to about 6,789 ETH by 16:00 UTC on October 19.
- At 16:00 UTC on Oct. 19, the liquidation estimate was about 1.7% above ETH's mid-price, with mark price controlling the trigger.
An unknown trader on Hyperliquid realized about $469,000 in losses before fees as an overnight Ethereum rebound forced the closure of nearly $19.8 million in ETH short exposure.
By the afternoon of Oct. 19, the wallet was adding to its bet against ETH again. Four new short orders between 13:56 and 14:04 UTC on Oct. 19 added about 1,126.2 ETH, worth roughly $2.7 million at execution.
By the 16:00 UTC account check, the wallet was short about 6,789.3 ETH, with the position valued near $16.2 million.
At 16:00 UTC on Oct. 19, that short used cross margin with leverage set to 25x. Hyperliquid estimated its liquidation price at about $2,434.67, while the venue's ETH mid-price immediately after the account check was about $2,393.05.
The trigger depends on mark price, which incorporates external exchange prices and Hyperliquid's order book. Funding payments and cross-margin account conditions can change the displayed liquidation estimate.
Hyperliquid's public fill data records 8,162.845 ETH of forced short closures across 632 execution fills. Those executions belonged to four partial liquidation groups between 23:27 UTC on Oct. 18 and 07:34 UTC on Oct. 19.
The $19.8 million total measures the ETH exposure closed at execution prices, while the roughly $469,000 realized loss is the trading result on those closures before fees and funding. It excludes any unrealized gain or loss on the short that remained open, so neither figure describes the account's complete trading result.
The wallet received 1,252,457.80 USDC at 15:19 UTC on Oct. 18, and opening short sales later that day traded near $2,366. The subsequent forced closures executed between about $2,409 and $2,445 as ETH rebounded, buying back exposure at higher prices than those entries.
On-chain analysis profile Lookonchain flagged the wallet's leveraged short in an Oct. 19 X post and later reported about 8,163 ETH of liquidations, worth $19.8 million.
Why the short survived the liquidations
Each of the four forced-close groups cut the then-current short by approximately one-fifth. After the final group at 07:34 UTC, the wallet still held a short of about 5,663.1 ETH. The trader later added another 1,126.2 ETH to that position.
Hyperliquid's partial liquidation rules explain how an account can retain exposure after a forced reduction. For a liquidatable position above 100,000 USDC, the venue initially sends 20% to the order book as a market liquidation order.
If a partial closure restores the account's maintenance-margin compliance, the trader can keep the remaining position and collateral.
Visible positions can become shared risk markers, especially public whale liquidation levels, which traders use as signals. Partial closures reduced the whale's short, then later orders increased it again.
Ethereum is +0.17% over the past 24 hours and currently sits at rank #2 by market cap.

articles.title: ESMA Adds BingX, YouHodler to MiCA Crypto Register
articles.text:
BingX, YouHodler added to ESMA MiCA register in latest update
ESMA’s latest MiCA register update includes BingX, YouHodler and Banco Santander’s Openbank, bringing the total to 375 unique CASPs.
[Update 11:30 UTC, Oct. 19 - Updates with comment from Penning Financial Services in the sixth paragraph.]
The European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) register added nine crypto-asset service providers (CASPs), including BingX, bringing the total to 375 unique providers.
The European Securities and Markets Authority’s (ESMA) Friday register update included crypto exchange BingX’s Austrian entity, MEGE zweite. It also listed the Italian subsidiary of YouHodler, a crypto lending platform offering yield products, with authorization for custody, crypto exchanges, order execution and transfers.
Both BingX and YouHodler announced their authorizations last week. BingX EU CEO Daniel Lai said the approval would allow the company to operate under a clear regulatory framework as it prepares to launch regulated services across the European Economic Area.
Other additions included Spain’s Prakma Markets, associated with the Goin crypto app, which operates a savings and investment platform.
Germany’s additions included Openbank Deutschland, a subsidiary of Spanish banking group Banco Santander, alongside cooperative lenders VR-Bank Alb-Blau-Donau and VR Bank im südlichen Franken.
Denmark’s Penning Financial Services is no longer listed, despite appearing in register updates dating back to July 3. A spokesperson for Penning told Cointelegraph that its MiCA authorization remains unchanged and that it had received no communication from Denmark’s financial regulator about any changes. Cointelegraph has contacted ESMA and Denmark’s Financial Supervisory Authority for clarification but had not received a response at the time of publication.
The e-money token (EMT) register was unchanged at 50 entries representing 25 unique entities, while the asset-referenced token (ART) register remained empty. The register of non-compliant crypto-asset service providers (NCASPs) increased by five entries to 178.

articles.title: JPMorgan's JPM Coin Arrives on Ethereum, Putting Bank Dollars on a Public Blockchain - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- JPMorgan launched JPM Coin on Ethereum for institutional clients, which can redeem the token for dollars at any time; it first launched on Coinbase's Base network in November 2025.
- The bank expects crypto firms to use the token for payments and financial institutions to use it to settle trades and post collateral, with only vetted counterparties allowed to hold it.
- Kinexys has handled over $4 trillion in transactions and about $7 billion a day, versus roughly $12 trillion a day across JPMorgan's payments business.
JPMorgan Chase is putting JPM Coin on Ethereum, which gives its biggest clients a way to move dollars in seconds on a Sunday night as easily as on a Tuesday morning.
A normal wire between banks only moves during business hours and can take days to land, which is why JPMorgan started experimenting with blockchain technology. The idea is using JPM Coin to cut that wait to seconds.
The token is a deposit token, so each unit stands for a dollar already sitting in a JPMorgan account, and the bank's site says clients can redeem it for dollars at any time with no lock-up. A stablecoin, by contrast, is a token pegged to the dollar by a private company that holds the reserves somewhere else.
Only vetted, approved counterparties can hold JPM Coin, so this is not a coin anyone can buy on an exchange.
JPMorgan first put the token on Base, a cheaper and faster network built on top of Ethereum and incubated by Coinbase, in November 2025. That followed months of testing with Mastercard and Coinbase, and holders can now move the token between the two networks.
In January, the bank also said it would bring JPM Coin to Canton Network, a privacy-focused blockchain built for financial markets. It has also issued two tokenized money-market funds on Ethereum, in December 2025 and May 2026, which are funds holding short-term debt that are represented as tokens.
Emma Landriault, global head of Kinexys Labs at JPMorgan's blockchain unit, pointed to the money and tokenized assets (traditional investments such as shares, debt and funds, issued as blockchain tokens) already circulating on Ethereum, where about $50 billion sits in applications, according to DefiLlama.
Crypto firms are expected to use the token for payments, while financial institutions can use it to pay for trades in tokenized assets or to post collateral, meaning a guarantee against a deal.
“We’ve clearly been in a year of further convergence between Wall Street and crypto,” Landriault told Bloomberg. Matthew Dawson, co-founder of Ethereum Institutional, called the move “a clear signal that institutional finance is moving onto public, verifiable infrastructure.”
The bank is also fighting for the same customers as stablecoin issuers. A consortium of more than 100 companies including Visa, Stripe, and Mastercard launched its own dollar stablecoin last month, while Kinexys co-head Naveen Mallela has said deposit tokens are “a compelling alternative” to stablecoins because they “can be yield-bearing,” meaning they can pay interest.
Kinexys, the unit behind the token, has handled more than $4 trillion in cumulative transactions and averages about $7 billion a day, against roughly $12 trillion a day across JPMorgan's wider payments business.
JPMorgan, Citigroup and other large banks plan to launch a shared 24/7 tokenized deposit network as early as the first half of 2027.

articles.title: France Advances Stablecoin Tax, Eyes Self-Custodial Wallets and Exit Tax Proposals
articles.text:
France advances stablecoin tax, eyes self-custodial wallets and exit tax proposals
France’s National Assembly adopted a crypto tax amendment targeting certain stablecoin swaps, while separate proposals on exit taxes and self-custodial wallet reporting remain under consideration.
French lawmakers narrowly approved a new crypto tax amendment on Friday that could make crypto-to-stablecoin swaps taxable events starting in 2027.
France’s National Assembly adopted Amendment I-3898 on Friday, with 38 votes in favor, 37 against and 25 abstentions. The measure was initially introduced as committee amendment I-CF1826 by French MP Nicolas Sansu and adopted on Oct. 7.
The Assembly is scheduled to vote on the first part of the 2027 Finance Bill on Tuesday, according to its official schedule. Other crypto-related proposals remain under consideration, although it is unclear whether each will be debated or voted on that day.
If enacted, the stablecoin amendment would tax certain crypto-to-stablecoin swaps and change how the country calculates crypto capital gains tax.
French National Assembly advances Amendment I-3898 on crypto-to-stablecoin tax swaps. Source: assemblee-nationale.fr
Under the proposal, investors converting their Bitcoin (BTC) or other cryptocurrencies into stablecoins would trigger a tax on the gains, even without converting gains into fiat. The calculation would use the acquisition cost of the sold crypto asset and the weighted average purchasing price.
Related: Deutsche Bank prepares German crypto custody launch, eyes Asia: Report
French lawmakers to discuss crypto exit tax, self-custodial wallet reporting measures
Separately, the Assembly rejected a proposal on Friday to carry forward realized crypto losses for 10 years, with 18 votes in favor, 75 against and 3 abstentions.
French lawmakers are preparing to discuss other crypto-related proposals as part of next year’s budget. Amendment I-CF1822 proposes to extend France’s exit tax regime to cover unrealized gains when taxpayers with aggregate crypto portfolio values exceeding €800,000 ($895,000) transfer their residences abroad.
Lawmakers are also weighing amendment I-2701, which would require individuals to declare the holdings of the self-custodial wallets if their total value exceeded €100,000 ($112,000) in the relevant tax year.
As of Monday, both proposals remain under consideration for the 2027 Finance Bill.
