articles.title: Scientists are unraveling the biggest genetic risk factor for Alzheimer's
articles.text:
A gene variant triples the risk of getting Alzheimer's disease — fat buildup in brain cells may be to blame, study finds
A gene variant called APOE4 is the biggest genetic risk factor for Alzheimer's disease. Scientists are finally figuring out how it works.
A gene variant called APOE4 dramatically increases the risk of late-onset Alzheimer's disease, the most common form of dementia. Now, emerging research is revealing APOE4's true role in the condition, and a new study pinpoints a possible way to treat it.
Historically, scientists studying Alzheimer's disease have focused on two proteins that accumulate in patients' brains: amyloid-beta and tau. However, there's a "third thing that people didn't pay attention to, until recently," said study co-author Li-Huei Tsai, a neuroscientist at MIT. That third thing is the accumulation of droplets of fat, or lipids, in the brain, she told Live Science.
The APOE gene makes proteins responsible for transporting fat around cells throughout the body and brain. A version of the gene called APOE4, which increases the risk of late-onset Alzheimer's three- to 12-fold, makes proteins that are less efficient at this function, Tsai said. But how APOE4 affects different brain cells was not clearly understood.
Tsai's team has been working to close that gap for about a decade.
"APOE4 can influence many different cell types," she emphasized. "It's not just one cell type."
Zeroing in on the clues
In past laboratory research, Tsai's team found that APOE4 causes a buildup of cholesterol in astrocytes, star-shaped brain cells that support the function of neurons. Genetic analyses suggested that the gene variant may mess with how these cells process fat.
Another study zoomed in on oligodendrocytes, cells that help insulate neurons' outgoing wires with a fatty material called myelin. This material helps neurons send messages more efficiently. APOE4 caused the oligodendrocytes to accumulate cholesterol. So, in lab mice, the team used a drug to help the cells get rid of that extra cholesterol, and it improved the cells' ability to make myelin and the mice's performance on cognitive tests.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
In their latest research, published Thursday (Oct. 15) in the journal Cell Stem Cell, Tsai's team dug into the question of why APOE4 causes fat to accumulate in the first place.
They used stem cells to grow APOE4-carrying oligodendrocytes and then turned specific genes on or off, to see if they increased or decreased the formation of fat droplets. This screening pointed to a major group of genes involved in cell-to-cell communication, called the Wnt signaling pathway. This included a key gene called DKK1, which acts as a brake on this signaling system.
Disabling DKK1 — essentially lifting the brake — reduced the concentration of fat droplets in the cells, the team found.
In brain tissue samples from organ donors with APOE4, the team also found signs of low Wnt signaling. This finding "establishes a very strong link" between the signaling pathway and formation of fat droplets, said Rosie Jackson, a cell biologist at the University of Dundee who was not involved in this study.
APOE4's effects across the brain
The researchers then investigated exactly how Wnt signaling was disrupted in oligodendrocytes.
APOE4 seemed to decrease the cells' supply of a protein that helps relay Wnt signals. That helpful protein was being broken down by an enzyme whose levels had been boosted by the APOE4. In mice, the team used a drug to block that extra enzyme, and the treatment ultimately restored normal Wnt signaling, reduced fat buildup, and helped the cells make myelin properly.
This could change how scientists think about treating Alzheimer's disease, Jackson said. It "opens up a new wave of potential therapeutics" that could target the accumulated fats, rather than going after only amyloid-beta and tau, she said.
"I think that this is becoming a really common idea in the field — that we're going to need multiple medications that target slightly different elements," she told Live Science. "And targeting lipids will be a really important part of that."
That said, the findings have not been confirmed in humans yet.
"It's very encouraging that facilitating lipid clearance and lipid movement is a potential therapeutic avenue," said study co-author Joel Blanchard, a neuroscientist at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai. The question is how we can do that in a safe and effective manner in humans, he said.
Related stories
Blanchard has led other research that underscores APOE4's effects beyond fats and myelin. The gene variant may affect cells that support blood vessels in the brain by driving scarring and contributing to amyloid-beta buildup. It may also mess with the "trash collectors" inside astrocytes, again leading to a buildup of harmful proteins.
While cells with other versions of the APOE gene can put a lot of energy toward breaking down the proteins, APOE4-carrying cells put all their energy toward fat storage, Blanchard said.
But more research is needed to understand how to fix the problem, he said. Hopefully, targeting fat storage "could rescue not just one thing but multiple things that go wrong in the course of Alzheimer's disease," he told Live Science.

articles.title: Hai cỗ xe ngựa bằng đồng lớn nhất trong lăng mộ Tần Thủy Hoàng sống động đến kinh ngạc
articles.text:
Một trong những phát hiện đáng kinh ngạc nhất trong lăng mộ Tần Thủy Hoàng, hoàng đế Trung Hoa đầu tiên, là hai cỗ xe ngựa được đúc bằng đồng.
Trang ccmap.cn chuyên giới thiệu về các di sản văn hóa Trung Quốc, gần đây đăng tải bài viết nhắc lại một trong những phát hiện đáng kinh ngạc nhất trong lăng mộ Tần Thủy Hoàng.
Năm 1980, trong một lần khai quật tại hố chôn ở phía Tây lăng mộ Tần Thủy Hoàng, các nhà khảo cổ Trung Quốc tìm thấy 2 cỗ xe ngựa bằng đồng lớn.
Hai cỗ xe ngựa này bị vỡ nát thành 3.000 mảnh, nhưng điều may mắn là tất cả các mảnh đều còn nguyên vẹn ở một chỗ, chưa bị đánh cắp hay bị xâm phạm.
Cỗ xe này được ví như chiếc xe giường nằm có điều hòa. Chiếc xe được thiết kế đa năng và tiện lợi.
Phải mất tới 8 năm phục chế, hai cỗ xe ngựa mới quay lại hình hài hoàn chỉnh và được đưa vào bảo tàng trưng bày.
Phần thân chính của 2 cỗ xe đều được làm bằng đồng, có một số bộ phận được làm bằng vàng và bạc. Mỗi một bộ phận đều được đúc riêng biệt, sau đó lắp ghép từ nhiều bộ phận lại với nhau.
Toàn thân ngựa kéo có màu trắng, được tạo thành từ loại bột màu khoáng trộn với keo dính đậm đặc. Kích thước của cỗ xe ngựa nhỏ bằng một nửa so với thực tế. Điều đáng ngạc nhiên là 2 cỗ xe này được làm cực kỳ chi tiết, mô phỏng rất chân thực.
Những con ngựa kéo được đúc một cách hết sức chi tiết.
Một xe ngựa được thiết kế để người ngồi hoặc đứng khi di chuyển. Chiếc xe ngựa còn lại có mái che. Hai cỗ xe có 2 bánh với 4 con ngựa kéo ở phía trước.
Theo các chuyên gia, cỗ xe thứ nhất dùng để mở đường. Trong khi đó, cỗ xe thứ hai là phương tiện để hoàng gia sử dụng, có cả giường nằm và "điều hòa". Bên trong chiếc xe có lót đệm mềm thêu hoa văn tinh xảo, sử gọi là "đệm văn". Khi chiếc xe này di chuyển, người ở bên trong có thể nằm hoặc ngồi, vừa sang trọng vừa thoải mái.
Toa xe bố trí cửa sổ hai lớp mở hất và trượt ngang. Hơn 2.000 năm sau, khi được khai quật, cửa sổ xe vẫn có thể mở ra kéo vào một cách trơn tru. Trên cửa sổ lớp ngoài còn có nhiều lỗ nhỏ, trong khi lớp cửa bên trong có thể đóng mở. Thiết kế này tạo ra hệ thống thông gió đặc biệt và giữ ấm cho xe. Hệ thống này cũng có tác dụng kiểm soát, điều chỉnh nhiệt độ ở trong xe.
Chiếc xe ngựa này có đệm nằm, có "điều hòa", nhưng điều khiến người ta ngạc nhiên hơn cả là xe còn có cả đường ray chuyên dụng. Theo các chuyên gia, để chiếc xe chạy êm và nhanh hơn, hoàng đế Tần Thủy Hoàng đã hạ lệnh xây dựng "trì đạo". Đây là đường ray dành cho xe ngựa của hoàng gia.
Trên thực tế, ở Nam Dương, tỉnh Hà Nam (Trung Quốc), các chuyên gia phát hiện dấu tích của "trì đạo" thời nhà Tần. Hóa ra vẫn còn đường ray gỗ và các thanh tà vẹt đều tăm tắp. Nhờ đường ray này nên xe ngựa chạy êm hơn. Đồng thời tà vẹt buộc ngựa phải chạy với tốc độ cao, bởi khoảng cách giữa các tà vẹt chính là khoảng cách bước chân ngựa. Theo đó, vó ngựa một khi đi vào đường ray sẽ tự động phi nhanh không ngừng cho tới khi đến được trạm dừng cố định.
Các bộ phận trên xe ngựa được làm rất tinh xảo, chính xác và sống động như thật. Thậm chí các vật dụng trên xe ngựa, đồ trang trí trên thân ngựa cũng như các bức tượng đều thể hiện rõ mục đích.
Kỹ thuật sơn màu trên đồ đồng đã cho thấy bước tiến đột phá của các nghệ nhân thời Tần, so với thời nhà Chu và thời Xuân Thu.
Cỗ xe ngựa bằng đồng được tìm thấy trong lăng mộ Tần Thủy Hoàng. Chiếc xe này được dùng để mở đường.
Hai cỗ xe ngựa bằng đồng trong lăng mộ Tần Thủy Hoàng được chính phủ Trung Quốc coi là di tích quốc gia cấp 1. Chúng được trưng bày tại bảo tàng lăng Tần Thủy Hoàng và là các cổ vật bị cấm đem ra nước ngoài.
Theo ccmapp.cn, cỗ xe ngựa bằng đồng thời nhà Tần là cỗ xe ngựa cổ lớn nhất, phức tạp nhất và hoàn chỉnh nhất từng được khai quật trong lịch sử Trung Quốc.

articles.title: A quantum highway just one atom high could transform superconductors
articles.text:
A quantum highway just one atom high could transform superconductors
- Date:
- October 16, 2026
- Source:
- Research Center for Materials Nanoarchitectonics (MANA)
- Summary:
- Scientists discovered that atomic steps just one atom high can guide quantum vortices through superconductors, making them move more than 1,000 times more easily in one direction than another. This remarkable control over quantum motion could lead to a new generation of ultra-efficient superconducting electronics.
- Share:
Scientists in Japan have discovered that tiny steps just one atom high can act like microscopic railroad tracks, guiding the movement of quantum vortices inside an ultrathin superconductor. Under certain conditions, these vortices moved more than 1,000 times more easily along the steps than across them. Researchers also found that they could adjust this remarkable effect simply by changing the temperature or magnetic field.
The discovery was made by researchers at the Research Center for Materials Nanoarchitectonics (MANA), part of Japan's National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS). Their findings offer a promising new approach to controlling quantum behavior and could eventually help engineers develop superconducting electronics that use far less energy while processing information more efficiently.
Why Controlling Quantum Vortices Matters
Superconductors are unusual materials that can carry electricity without electrical resistance when cooled below a critical temperature. This property makes them attractive for developing extremely energy-efficient electronics and other advanced technologies.
However, superconductors also contain tiny quantum structures known as vortices. These form where magnetic fields penetrate the material, creating small regions surrounded by circulating electrical currents. When the vortices move, they can generate electrical resistance and affect the performance of the superconductor.
Being able to control where these vortices travel could therefore help scientists improve superconducting devices. Until now, directing their movement in extremely thin, two-dimensional superconductors has been particularly difficult.
To investigate this challenge, a team led by Takashi Uchihashi at MANA studied an ultrathin superconductor whose surface contained a series of regularly spaced atomic steps. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, a technique capable of imaging surfaces at the atomic level, the researchers confirmed that the steps ran parallel to one another and directly observed vortices positioned along them.
The findings were published in the journal Physical Review B.
Atomic Steps Act Like Rails for Quantum Motion
The experiments revealed an extraordinary difference in how easily the vortices could move depending on their direction.
Using four-terminal resistance measurements, which allow researchers to precisely measure electrical resistance, the team found that vortices traveled more than 1,000 times more easily along the atomic steps than across them when exposed to intermediate magnetic fields.
In effect, the steps acted like tiny rails, creating preferred pathways for quantum vortices to follow.
"Our study shows that atomic-scale steps can act as effective rails that guide superconducting vortices, and that this guiding effect can be tuned simply by changing the temperature or magnetic field," said Uchihashi.
The researchers also identified a particularly interesting behavior when the magnetic field ranged from approximately 0.10 to 0.20 T (tesla, a unit used to measure magnetic field strength). Within this range, vortices could flow freely along the steps without becoming trapped by imperfections in the material.
This behavior, known as one-dimensional pinning-free vortex flow, means the vortices can travel along a defined path without encountering the usual obstacles that restrict their movement.
At the lowest temperatures, the researchers observed another unusual effect. Vortex motion was governed by quantum tunneling, a phenomenon in which quantum objects can pass through energy barriers that would normally prevent their movement under classical physics.
A New Path Toward More Efficient Superconductors
The findings demonstrate that even a surface feature only one atom high can have a powerful influence on the movement of quantum vortices.
By using these atomic steps as natural guiding tracks, scientists may be able to control vortex motion with remarkable precision. The ability to adjust that motion through temperature and magnetic fields also provides an additional way to influence how superconductors behave.
Although practical applications will require further development, this atomic-scale approach could eventually help researchers manage both vortex movement and heat flow in future superconducting technologies, potentially enabling more efficient devices that consume less power.

Journal Reference:
- Wenxuan Qian, Yash Chauhan, Ryohei Nemoto, Keisuke Sagisaka, Shunsuke Yoshizawa, Takashi Uchihashi. Anisotropic transport of Josephson vortices in atomic-layer superconductors on vicinal surfaces. Physical Review B, 2026; 114 (5) DOI: 10.1103/b2j3-xj19

articles.title: World's fastest AI-powered racing drone outflies the best human pilots
articles.text:
World's fastest AI-powered racing drone outflies the best human pilots
An AI-operated drone learned to fly from scratch and navigated a race course at speeds over 60 mph, using a single camera.
A drone powered by artificial intelligence (AI) has completed a championship race course faster than some of the world's best human drone pilots.
In a study published Oct. 14 in the journal Science Robotics, scientists created an AI system capable of pushing a quadcopter through a demanding course at over 60 mph (100 km/h), using little more than a single forward-facing camera, an inertial measurement unit, and a tiny onboard computer.
The system, called MonoRace, even won the 2025 Abu Dhabi Autonomous Racing League drone racing competition, outperforming every rival autonomous team and posting faster times than three former human world-champion drone pilots.
MonoRace accomplished this without the aid of GPS, external motion-capture systems, stereo cameras, or a preloaded map of the course. The system is an onboard autonomous flight model created by researchers at the Delft University of Technology's Micro Air Vehicles Lab in the Netherlands. Its name reflects its central design feature; "mono" refers to its monocular vision. The drone relies on a single rolling shutter camera and monitors its own motion with an internal measurement unit (IMU) that gauges acceleration and rotation.
Flying at breakneck speeds
The limited sensor package feeds a neural network, a machine-learning model that uses interconnected artificial neurons to learn patterns from data. This neural network identifies racing gates and estimates the drone's position and motion to generate motor commands. Then, it sends the commands to the four propellers at a rate of 500 times per second through the drone's flight controller.
The system fits a drone that weighs a mere 966 grams (2.13 pounds) and measures approximately 11.8 x 11 x 3.9 inches (30 x 28 x 10 centimeters). Because the MonoRace hardware was so compact, lightweight and computationally efficient, the team was able to operate it entirely aboard the drone.
On the Abu Dhabi course, MonoRace completed two laps around 11 gates in 16.56 seconds, hitting a top speed of approximately 63 mph (102 km/h).
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
A recently released video tracks MonoRace's development and performance in the competition, with real flight sequences demonstrating how the drone banks sharply, accelerates through gates, and navigates a course without human assistance.
However, some of the sequences are computer-generated. Study co-author Guido de Croon, a professor at the Delft University of Technology, said those are intentional visual effects. The only fully simulated imagery appears at about the two-minute mark, during the segment showing the training process.
"Here we show the gates in a visual simulator for the video but the real training happened in a stripped-down, pure physics simulator that ran really fast," de Croon told Live Science in an email. "Simulating vision was not done during training, as the control neural network receives an estimated state as input, which comes from a different perception and state estimation process."
The rest of the footage is real, although some shots include overlays showing how the drone interprets its camera feed. A convolutional neural network segments the white gates, sometimes displaying them as red in the normal camera image. Small circles mark detected gate corners, red lines indicate gate edges, and a blue overlay shows the portion of the image where the drone expects to find the next gate.
How the AI learned to race
Scientists trained the MonoRace model with reinforcement learning, a machine learning method in which an agent repeatedly attempts a task and receives feedback based on its success or failure.
"The reinforcement learning ran in simulation, because it needs lots of trial and error — like millions of tries," de Croon said. "It actually learns to fly from scratch."
The network learned to translate the drone's position on the track, velocity and orientation directly into motor commands. According to de Croon, early training focused on the basics, like avoiding crashes and reaching the first gate. As the training progressed, the system learned to advance farther along the course and fly at higher speeds.
The researchers didn't train the system on a single aircraft. Instead, they varied dimensions such as weight, voltage, drag, sensor noise and propeller condition so the AI model could cope with real-world variations and imperfections.
"That ensures that the trained network can control different drones," de Croon said.
Related stories
MonoRace could become a training tool for human drone pilots, "a bit like powerful chess programs have also inspired humans playing the game," de Croon said.
Its broader significance lies in demonstrating advancements in physical AI, especially how a robot can perceive, decide and act at high speeds despite limited sensing and computing power. The control network runs on a microcontroller-class chip, meaning that sophisticated control doesn't require a large computer.
De Croon noted that a similarly sized network could optimize for minimal energy use rather than minimum lap time. Because most machines rely on small processors and conventional controllers, energy-optimal neural control could eventually reduce power consumption in everyday robotics, he said.
Bahnam, S. A., Ferede, R., Blaha, T. M., Lang, A. E., Lucassen, E., Missinne, Q., Verraest, A. E. C., De Wagter, C., & De Croon, G. C. H. E. (2026). MonoRace: Robust monocular AI for champion-level drone racing. Science Robotics, 11(119). https://doi.org/10.1126/scirobotics.aee9250
Alan is a freelance tech and entertainment journalist who specializes in computers, laptops, and video games. He's previously written for sites like PC Gamer, GamesRadar, and Rolling Stone. If you need advice on tech, or help finding the best tech deals, Alan is your man.

articles.title: “Crawzilla” was huge. Then scientists found an even bigger crayfish
articles.text:
“Crawzilla” was huge. Then scientists found an even bigger crayfish
- Date:
- October 15, 2026
- Source:
- College of ACES at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
- Summary:
- A nationwide search for giant crayfish uncovered a record-breaking Tennessee specimen and a surprising mystery about how big these freshwater creatures can grow. Scientists found that North American crayfish seem to hit a biological size limit, possibly because of their muscles or protective shells.
- Share:
A giant crayfish nicknamed "Crawzilla" has sparked an unexpected scientific discovery, revealing a possible biological limit to how large North America's crayfish can grow.
The investigation began when Caitlin Bloomer pulled an enormous Crawzilla crawdad from the mud during a biological survey in Kentucky. Crawzilla is the creature's actual common name, and Bloomer was convinced she had captured the largest crayfish ever documented. But when she proudly showed her discovery to a colleague, the reaction was not quite what she expected.
"I thought, 'There's no doubt I have caught the biggest crayfish anyone's ever seen!' I brought it back to campus to show my colleague, naturally bragging about having caught the biggest-ever crayfish. But, as all biologists and sport fishermen do, he took one look and said, 'No way, I've caught bigger,'" said Bloomer, a teaching assistant professor in the Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Sciences within the College of Agricultural, Consumer and Environmental Sciences at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.
A Nationwide Hunt for North America's Biggest Crayfish
What started as a little friendly rivalry soon turned into a nationwide search for record-breaking crayfish. Bloomer contacted biologists and museum curators across the country, asking them to examine their collections for unusually large specimens.
Using calipers, instruments designed to measure objects with great precision, the researchers compared the sizes of preserved crayfish. Their search produced a list of 20 exceptionally large individuals representing 18 different species. The results were published in the scientific journal Ecology.
Although Bloomer's original Crawzilla did not claim the top spot, it still earned a place among the largest specimens identified.
"Mine was not the biggest, but it did make the top 20, so I'm super proud of it," Bloomer said. "And it was also the only burrowing crayfish to make the list, so I'll take the win."
Scientists Identify the Largest Known North American Crayfish
The biggest specimen belonged to a Tennessee bottlebrush crayfish preserved in the collection at West Liberty University in West Virginia. It measured an impressive 86.6 millimeters, or approximately 3.4 inches, excluding its tail, claws, and antennae.
The record-holder was not a recent catch. It had been collected in 2011 by Dr. Zac Loughman and students from West Liberty University, making the discovery possible through the examination of existing museum specimens.
"I knew we had some massive crayfish in the West Liberty University Astacology Collection, but it was a surprise to learn we had the two largest specimens known from North America! Our record-holder, a Tennessee bottlebrush crayfish collected by Dr. Zac Loughman and West Liberty students back in 2011, shows just how amazing and diverse crayfish can be," said Zackary Graham, an assistant professor of biology at West Liberty University. "Its carapace alone is about the length of a credit card, and with the tail and claws, it stretches nearly the width of a sheet of notebook paper. Both of these giants are now proudly displayed in my office, and I show them to just about everyone who walks in."
Other institutions also contributed impressive specimens. The Illinois Natural History Survey, which belongs to the Prairie Research Institute at the University of Illinois, accounted for six of the 20 largest crayfish. The Smithsonian Institution's National Museum of Natural History contributed another four.
Why Can't North American Crayfish Grow Even Bigger?
Beyond settling the competition, the researchers uncovered a more intriguing scientific question. Their measurements provided some of the first estimates of the upper size limits for North American crayfish, and the results suggested that these animals may face a surprisingly consistent growth ceiling.
Despite differences among species and environments, the largest individuals tended to reach roughly 80 millimeters in the body measurement used by the researchers. That raised an obvious question: Why do North American crayfish appear to stop growing at around this size when some species elsewhere in the world, including the Tasmanian giant freshwater crayfish, can become dramatically larger?
"They all seemed to max out around that 80-millimeter mark, but we weren't sure why, especially given that there are absolutely massive crayfish in other parts of the world," Bloomer said. "We started looking at things like latitude, oxygen availability, and habitat type as possible correlates to explain why certain species and individuals were larger than others, but we weren't seeing any patterns."
The team examined whether geographic location, oxygen levels, or the type of environment where a crayfish lives could explain why some grow larger than others. However, none of these factors showed a clear relationship with maximum body size.
That unexpected result pointed the researchers toward a different possibility. Rather than being primarily controlled by environmental conditions, crayfish growth may be constrained by the animals' own biology.
One potential explanation involves their exoskeletons, the hard outer coverings that protect their bodies. Differences in shell structure or muscle anatomy might impose physical limits on how large North American crayfish can become.
For now, that remains a hypothesis. Further research will be needed to determine whether these biological features actually restrict their growth.
"This was a case where we saw something unusual in the field and it sparked a future research direction," Bloomer said. "We think that it could really be worthwhile to look at the physiology of crayfish to see if something there is influencing their body size."
Giant Crayfish Reveal How Much Scientists Still Don't Know
Crayfish are familiar inhabitants of streams, rivers, and other freshwater environments. Many people encounter them as children, making them among the most recognizable aquatic animals in North America.
Yet even with their widespread presence, scientists are still discovering basic facts about their biology, including how large they can grow and what determines their maximum size.
"Anyone that goes to a stream as a kid knows what crayfish are -- they're almost a universal onboarding for people to care about aquatic life. I still go out with people who are in their 50s or 60s, who recall catching crawfish in the creek when they were seven," Bloomer said. "It's just amazing how much we still have to learn about them."
Bloomer also emphasized that the investigation would not have been possible without museum collections. By comparing specimens preserved over many years, researchers were able to answer a fundamental question that would have been difficult to investigate through fieldwork alone.
What began with one unusually large crayfish and a disagreement between colleagues has now opened a new line of scientific inquiry into the biological factors that shape the size of these familiar freshwater creatures.

Shoobs, Christopher A. Taylor, Eric R. Larson. North American crayfish: A quest for the biggest catch. Ecology, 2026; 107 (9) DOI: 10.1002/ecy.70471

articles.title: “Rụng rời chân tay” với những chiếc cầu thang “tử thần” ít ai dám bước lên
articles.text:
Những chiếc cầu thang này không dành cho người sợ độ cao.
Bức ảnh selfie đòi hỏi sự can đảm.
Đứng vững được trên chiếc cầu thang này đã là một thành công.
Vừa bước đi vừa cầu nguyện.
Chiếc cầu thang không dành cho người chân ngắn?
Những căn hộ phía trên có mở cửa toang hoác cũng chẳng tên nào dám mò lên chiếc cầu thang này mà ăn trộm.
Trượt chân một cái là xác định "đăng xuất" khỏi Trái đất như chơi...
Người dám trèo lên chiếc thang này hẳn đã gạt bỏ mọi khái niệm về sự nguy hiểm.
Hãy thầm cầu mong đừng có cơn gió lớn nào thổi qua khi bước trên chiếc thang này.

articles.title: 'Cute demo, but totally impractical': Experts are skeptical that Tesla's 'Rocket' Roadster could actually work in the real world
articles.text:
'Cute demo, but totally impractical': Experts are skeptical that Tesla's 'Rocket' Roadster could actually work in the real world
Tesla has unveiled a new version of its Roadster EV that can briefly take to the air using SpaceX tech. Whether it actually qualifies as a flying car is another matter.
Tesla has unveiled a new "flying" version of its Roadster electric vehicle (EV) that uses SpaceX tech to pull off seemingly impressive airborne acrobatics.
During a filmed demonstration at the SpaceX rocket testing facility in Texas Thursday (Oct. 15), the second-generation Tesla Roadster was shown accelerating up a curved ramp before launching itself into the air, performing a 180-degree barrel roll and touching back down to Earth.
In another stunt, the vehicle leapt over a row of parked Teslas. For safety reasons, the vehicle was operated remotely in both instances.
"Turns out, the future does have flying cars," Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk wrote on X following the demonstration.
The Roadster's airborne capabilities are made possible by a system of cold-gas thrusters developed using technology from Musk's aerospace company, SpaceX. These thrusters release bursts of high-pressure gas to generate thrust, allowing the vehicle to accelerate rapidly and, according to Tesla, become airborne for short periods.
The new Roadster will come in three variants: Performance, Thrust and Rocket. Only the Rocket is capable of flight. The Performance model is a two-seater equipped with a suction system that's designed to improve traction and handling (or drive up inverted ramps, as in Tesla's demo), while the Thrust model adds rear-mounted thrusters that Tesla claims can propel the vehicle from 0 to 60 mph (97 km/h) in under a second.
The highest-end model, Rocket, features SpaceX cold-gas thrusters positioned around the vehicle to enable short bursts of flight and in-air control. This single-seat model will be available by invitation only, according to Tesla.
On the company's website, Tesla representatives explicitly stated that the Rocket isn't approved for use on public roads and that availability depends on regional regulations. During the reveal, Musk told the audience that the Rocket "is not necessarily a safety-optimized car."
Tesla hasn't disclosed how far or for how long its EV can remain airborne, nor is it the first company to develop a hybrid road-air vehicle. There is also skepticism from outside viewers on whether the demonstration could be replicated outside of controlled scenarios.
Artificial intelligence (AI) scientist Yann LeCun — a professor of data science, computer science, neural science and electrical engineering at New York University — described the demonstration on X as a "marketing stunt" and questioned whether the vehicle would work in practice.
"Even assuming that 50% of the mass of the car is the compressed air, that gives you less than 10s of useful thrust (with thrust-to-weight ratio larger than 1.0). Probably more like 5 seconds, actually," he posted on the social media platform. "So the car must be an empty, lightweight shell containing big compressed air tanks. Cute demo, but totally impractical. But of course, you knew that."
He likened it to SpaceShipOne, which debuted in 2004 as the first privately funded spacecraft and made three record-setting flights before being retired.
California-based Alef Aeronautics, which is developing its own flying EVs, marked Tesla's unveiling by releasing footage of its vehicle flying over an earlier Roadster model. Alef representatives said the demonstration marked its 1,000th logged flight.
Exclusive to Live Science Pro
"Welcome Tesla to the flying car race, we've been here alone for eleven years," Alef CEO Jim Dukhovny said in a statement emailed to Live Science. "Having competition is a good thing, especially from such a major company as Tesla."
Unlike Tesla's compressed-gas tech, Alef's vehicle uses electric propellers for vertical takeoff and landing, with a rotating cabin and body designed to support forward flight.
Production of the new Roadster is scheduled for 2028, but Tesla doesn't have the best track record of meeting its deadlines. The company has delayed production of its Optimus humanoid robot a few times since first unveiling the machine in 2021, for example, with an initial start in 2023, before being pushed back. Only in recent months has production begun to scale to a few hundred units per week.

Owen Hughes is a freelance writer and editor specializing in data and digital technologies. Previously a senior editor at ZDNET, Owen has been writing about tech for more than a decade, during which time he has covered everything from AI, cybersecurity and supercomputers to programming languages and public sector IT. Owen is particularly interested in the intersection of technology, life and work – in his previous roles at ZDNET and TechRepublic, he wrote extensively about business leadership, digital transformation and the evolving dynamics of remote work.

articles.title: Antarctica’s sea ice has undergone a stunning reversal
articles.text:
Antarctica’s sea ice has undergone a stunning reversal
- Date:
- October 15, 2026
- Source:
- NASA Earth Observatory
- Summary:
- Antarctic sea ice reached its third-lowest winter maximum in 2026, extending a remarkable decline that began after years of record-breaking growth. Scientists are investigating whether the dramatic reversal signals a long-term shift in Antarctica's frozen landscape.
- Share:
Antarctic sea ice reached its annual winter peak in September 2026, but the ice covered less ocean than in nearly any other year since satellite measurements began. Its maximum extent was the third lowest on record, adding to growing evidence of a dramatic shift in Antarctica's frozen waters.
Antarctica is surrounded by a vast ocean, giving its sea ice plenty of room to spread outward during the Southern Hemisphere's winter. This differs from the Arctic, where an ocean basin is enclosed by surrounding land. Although Antarctica's geography allows winter sea ice to expand over enormous distances, it also pushes the ice into warmer latitudes, where melting becomes more likely during summer. As a result, Antarctic sea ice generally reaches its largest extent in September before shrinking to its annual minimum in February.
According to NASA and the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC), Antarctic sea ice likely reached its annual maximum extent on September 14 (above). At its peak, the ice stretched across approximately 17.59 million square kilometers (6.79 million square miles). That made 2026 the year with the third-lowest winter maximum in the satellite record.
The maps below illustrate how Antarctic sea ice changes between seasons, showing average ice concentrations in September (left) and the following February (right) from 1990 to 2026. Solid white regions represent areas with the greatest ice coverage, while dark blue indicates open ocean. Only locations where ice covers at least 15 percent of the water are included. Scientists use this threshold to determine which areas qualify as ice-covered when calculating the total "sea ice extent."
Antarctic Sea Ice Shifts From Record Growth to Historic Lows
For decades, Antarctic sea ice appeared to be moving in the opposite direction from the rapidly shrinking ice in the Arctic. Between 1979 and 2014, sea ice extent around Antarctica increased by approximately 1 percent per decade. However, because Antarctic ice coverage naturally fluctuates considerably from year to year, researchers remain uncertain whether this gradual increase reflected a meaningful long-term change.
The expansion became particularly noticeable between 2012 and 2014, when Antarctic winter sea ice set new record highs for three consecutive years. These records stood in stark contrast to conditions at the opposite pole, where Arctic sea ice was undergoing a steep decline.
But Antarctica's upward trend ended in 2015. Beginning in 2016, the region experienced substantial losses in sea ice coverage, marking a striking reversal from the preceding decades. Although some years have brought modest recoveries, Antarctic sea ice has generally remained below its historical average.
The most extreme conditions occurred in 2023, when Antarctica recorded both its lowest summer minimum and its lowest winter maximum since satellite observations began. The unusually low maximum in 2026 adds another significant measurement to this changing picture. Scientists are continuing to track the ice each year to determine whether these declines represent a lasting transformation in Antarctic sea ice conditions or fall within the range of statistical variability.
How Satellites Track Antarctic Sea Ice Through Clouds
Scientists measure Antarctic sea ice using satellites equipped with instruments called passive microwave sensors. Rather than relying on visible light, these instruments detect microwave energy naturally emitted by Earth's surface.
Sea ice produces a stronger microwave signal than open ocean water, allowing researchers to distinguish frozen areas from ice-free seas. An important advantage of this approach is that microwaves can pass through clouds. This means scientists can repeatedly observe Antarctic sea ice even when thick cloud cover prevents conventional satellite cameras from seeing the surface.
The long-running satellite record began in late 1978 with observations from NASA's Nimbus-7 spacecraft. Starting in 1987, satellites operated under the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) contributed additional measurements. NASA's Aqua satellite also provided data between 2002 and 2011.
The monitoring effort continues to evolve as satellite technology changes. In 2025, researchers began incorporating observations from the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency's GCOM-W satellite, helping maintain the decades-long record used to understand Antarctica's changing ice.
NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using data from the National Snow and Ice Data Center.

articles.title: Bí quyết giúp phi công Mỹ có thể ngủ chỉ trong 2 phút mà ai cũng có thể học
articles.text:
Winter cho rằng một khi cơ thể ta đã vào trạng thái thư giãn, ta có thể “gạt mọi suy nghĩ liên quan đến hoạt động ra khỏi tâm trí chỉ trong 10 giây thì ta sẽ ngủ được”.
Có bao giờ bạn muốn tranh thủ chợp mắt trong chốc lát không? Dù bạn đã chọn một tư thế thoải mái trên ghế hoặc trong góc phòng, nhắm mắt lại nhưng vẫn tỉnh. Dù cảm thấy khá mệt, bạn vẫn không ngủ được, giờ nghỉ đã hết mà bạn thì chẳng chợp mắt được phút nào. Bạn không chỉ không ngủ được mà còn chẳng tranh thủ làm được việc gì cả.
Không phải ai cũng có thể ngủ ngay khi mình muốn. Ngay cả việc ngủ được khi vừa đặt mình xuống giường mỗi đêm đã rất khó khăn rồi.
Nhưng có một kỹ năng giúp bạn có thể ngủ trong 2 phút mà ai cũng có thể học được. Bài tập này được xây dựng trong thời kỳ Chiến tranh Thế giới II cho các phi công hải quân.
Khi Chiến tranh Thế giới II bắt đầu được vài năm, đội quân Hoa Kỳ nhận ra một vấn đề cần giải quyết ngay.
Vì áp lực cực lớn của các trận không chiến, nhiều phi công của họ bị căng thẳng đến mức không kịp phản ứng khi đang bay và phạm phải những sai lầm chết người như bắn nhầm quân mình hoặc gặp phải tai nạn hoàn toàn tránh được.
Ngủ là trạng thái thả lỏng cả về cơ thể lẫn tâm trí.
Để giảm tổn thất, đội quân Hoa Kỳ đã nhờ Thiếu úy Hải quân Bud Winter nghiên cứu và thử nghiệm một phương pháp khoa học giúp thư giãn. Mục tiêu của chương trình là dạy cho các phi công cách thư giãn để họ có thể học tập và phản ứng nhanh hơn, tăng cường sự tập trung và đánh tan nỗi sợ hãi.
Khóa huấn luyện cũng dạy cho các phi công biết cách thiếp đi trong vòng 2 phút vào bất kỳ lúc nào, bất kể ngày đêm, trong bất kỳ tình huống nào. Kỹ thuật này có kèm theo hướng dẫn để đảm bảo các phi công được ngủ đủ giấc và có thể tranh thủ chợp mắt một chút mỗi khi có thể.
Để đạt mục tiêu đầu tiên, Winter đã dạy các phi công cách thư giãn có thể. Để đạt mục tiêu thứ hai, ông dạy họ cách thư giãn tâm trí. Trên thực tế, Winter đã định nghĩa việc ngủ là trạng thái thả lỏng cả về cơ thể lẫn tâm trí. Để ngủ ngay khi mình muốn, trước hết bạn phải biết cách thư giãn cơ thể, sau đó là thư giãn tâm trí.
Trong cuốn sách Relax and Win viết về chương trình được xây dựng cho các phi công chiến đấu, Winter đã ghi lại chính xác những hướng dẫn ông dạy các phi công tập cách thư giãn cơ thể:
"Ngồi xuống ghế, đặt 2 bàn chân lên sàn. Đầu gối mở, 2 tay thả lỏng đặt trong lòng. Hãy nhắm mắt lại, gục đầu xuống cho đến khi cằm chạm ngực.
Hít thở đều và sâu một cách chậm rãi. Không được nhăn trán, thả lỏng da đầu. Tiếp theo, thả lỏng hàm và để miệng hở một cách tự nhiên. Thả lỏng các cơ mặt, cả lưỡi và môi. Không bặm hay mím môi. Hít thở chậm.
Giờ thì hãy thả lỏng để vai rũ xuống thấp hết mức có thể. Bạn có cảm thấy phần cơ sau cổ được thả lỏng không? Hãy thư giãn phần cổ hết mức.
Tiếp theo, hãy thư giãn ngực. Hít một hơi thật sâu rồi nín thở. Sau đó thở mạnh, đẩy tất cả căng thẳng ra khỏi lồng ngực cho ngực xẹp lại. Hít thở chậm. Khi thở ra, hãy đẩy căng thẳng ra bên ngoài.
Tiếp theo thả lỏng các cơ cánh tay. Đầu tiên là bắp tay phải, rồi đến cẳng tay phải, sau đó là bàn tay và ngón tay phải. Bạn phải cảm thấy tay mình như được buông thõng hoàn toàn. Lặp lại quá trình thư giãn với tay trái. Hít thở chậm.
Giờ thì toàn bộ thân trên của bạn đã được thư giãn, cảm giác ấm áp dễ chịu đang lan tỏa khắp người bạn. Bạn thấy rất thoải mái. Một cảm giác hạnh phúc nảy nở trong lòng.
Tiếp theo là thư giãn thân dưới. Thả lỏng cơ đùi phải. Bạn phải cảm thấy đùi hoàn toàn được buông thõng. Tiếp đến là thả lỏng bắp chân, cổ chân rồi bàn chân. Lặp lại quá trình thư giãn với chân trái, bắt đầu từ đùi, rồi đến bắp chân, cổ chân và bàn chân.
Lúc này, toàn thân bạn đã được thư giãn hoàn toàn. Để chắc chắn hơn, hãy hít thở sâu 3 nhịp và khi thở ra, hãy đẩy tất cả những căng thẳng còn lại ra ngoài".
Nếu bạn không thể thư giãn một bộ phận nào đó thì hãy thử gồng lên trước rồi mới thả lỏng.
Khi làm theo quy trình trên, cơ thể bạn có thể được thả lỏng ở một mức độ tương đối. Winter đã dạy cho các phi công cách đạt được trạng thái này trong bất kỳ tình huống căng thẳng nào. Nó sẽ giúp họ thả lỏng, giảm căng thẳng, tăng cường tập trung và đưa ra quyết định sáng suốt hơn.
Từ trạng thái cơ thể được thư giãn này, Winter bắt đầu dạy cho các phi công tập sự cách "thiếp đi và có một giấc ngủ sâu thoải mái" bằng cách thư giãn tâm trí hoàn toàn.
Winter cho rằng môt khi cơ thể ta đã vào trạng thái thư giãn, ta có thể "gạt mọi suy nghĩ liên quan đến hoạt động ra khỏi tâm trí chỉ trong 10 giây thì ta sẽ ngủ được". Vì vậy, để thiếp đi nhanh, bạn cần ngăn những dòng suy nghĩ chạy đi chạy lại trong đầu bạn. Bạn phải ngừng suy nghĩ về những lo âu, hối tiếc và các vấn đề hiện tại.
Winter đặc biệt nhấn mạnh là không được có những suy nghĩ liên quan đến hoạt động. Dù việc dùng trí tưởng tượng để "tập thể dục tại chỗ" sẽ đem lại cho ta một vài lợi ích, nhưng những suy nghĩ này sẽ làm tăng cơ và gây khó ngủ.
Vậy, khi bạn muốn ngủ, hãy chỉ nghĩ đến những hình ảnh tĩnh lặng và yên bình nhất. Dưới đây là 3 hình ảnh mà Winter đề xuất. Bạn không nhất thiết phải dùng hết cả 3, hãy chọn 1 trong 3 và nếu không hiệu quả thì đổi qua cái khác:
"Với hình ảnh 1, hãy tưởng tượng một ngày mùa xuân ấm áp, bạn đang nằm trên một chiếc xuồng trên mặt hồ phẳng lặng. Bạn đang nhìn lên bầu trời xanh biếc với những áng mây bay. Đừng để bất kỳ suy nghĩ nào khác len vào. Hãy chỉ tập trung vào hình ảnh này và chặn những suy nghĩ khác ở bên ngoài tâm trí, đặc biệt là những suy nghĩ có liên quan đến vận động. Hãy tận hưởng khung cảnh yên bình này trong 10 giây.
Với hình ảnh 2, hãy tưởng tượng bạn đang nằm trên một cái võng nhung lớn màu đen và xung quanh đều là bóng tối. Bạn phải giữ hình ảnh này trong tâm trí trong 10 giây.
Mẹo thứ ba là lặp đi lặp lại câu "không nghĩ… không nghĩ… không nghĩ". Giữ trạng thái này và đẩy những suy nghĩ khác ra khỏi đầu trong ít nhất 10 giây".
Sau 6 tuần luyện tập, 96% phi công đã có thể thiếp đi chỉ trong vòng 2 phút - ở bất cứ nơi đâu và bất cứ lúc nào. Không chỉ vậy, họ thậm chí còn có thể ngủ được khi đã uống cà phê và ngay cả khi xung quanh là tiếng máy và pháo giả.
Bạn có thể dùng phương pháp thư giãn chung này để thư giãn cơ thể bất kỳ khi nào thấy căng thẳng. Sau đó hãy thực hiện bài tập thư giãn tâm trí khi bạn muốn sớm thiếp đi. Bài tập này sẽ hữu ích khi bạn muốn chợp mắt trong chốc lát. Winter cho rằng, ngay cả một giấc ngủ dài 5 phút cũng giúp ta hồi phục rất nhiều. Bạn cũng có thể dùng kỹ thuật này để "ngủ gật", một dạng ngủ cực ngắn để kích thích óc sáng tạo trong ranh giới giữa ngủ với thức. Hoặc đơn giản là bạn dùng kỹ thuật này khi để đi vào giấc ngủ nhanh và sâu hơn.
Hãy nhớ rằng khả năng thư giãn cơ thể và tâm trí cũng là một kỹ năng. Như mọi kỹ năng khác, bạn sẽ không thể thành công chỉ sau một vài lần thử. Bạn phải tập đi tập lại đến khi quen với việc thư giãn. Bạn sẽ thành công nếu chịu khó rèn luyện thói quen này một cách thường xuyên.

articles.title: Romans may have set fire to Celtic town during conquest to 'humiliate' enemy, archaeologists find
articles.text:
Romans may have set fire to Celtic town during conquest to 'humiliate' the enemy, archaeologists find
Archaeologists discovered a first-century-B.C. military camp that was erected during Emperor Augustus' Cantabrian Wars.
Archaeologists have unearthed a Roman military camp in Spain, where they found fragments of weapons and metal tacks from soldiers' shoes. The camp was used during the Cantabrian Wars fought by Emperor Augustus as he expanded the Roman Empire in the first century B.C.
The fortified military camp is made up of an earthen platform roughly 39 feet (12 meters) wide, which is surrounded by a stone perimeter wall about 5 feet (1.5 m) thick, according to a translated statement. Uncovered during excavations earlier this year, the camp is situated about one-third of a mile (500 m) from where an Iron Age settlement was once inhabited by the Cantabri people, a group of Celtic tribes that lived among the Cantabrian Mountains in modern-day northern Spain.
The Cantabri fiercely resisted Roman rule for a decade, but in 19 B.C., they were conquered by the military commanded by Emperor Augustus. The Cantabrian Wars marked the end of local control over the territory, as the Iberian Peninsula then came under control of the Roman Empire.
"It's not easy to find a camp associated with a hill fort in this condition," Eduardo González Gómez de Agüero, an archaeologist at the University of León who co-directed the excavation project, said in the statement.
Among the well-preserved remains at the camp were metal weapon fragments and small iron tacks known as hobnails, which were hammered into the bottom of Roman soldiers' leather military sandals to help provide traction on rocky and muddy terrain. These objects are evidence that the Roman military was prepared to attack and subdue the Iron Age community, according to the statement.
The archaeologists also uncovered evidence of a major fire that destroyed most of the pre-Roman settlement, including two temples. González Gómez de Agüero suggested that the Romans may have deliberately set the fire as part of their conquest.
RELATED STORIES
"It's not just about defeating the enemy, but about humiliating them, erasing their identity, and breaking their connection to the land," he said in the statement.
Researchers are still working on establishing the chronology of the Romans' final attack on the Cantabri and want to understand if the settlement was destroyed in a single event or over time. Previously, another research team found 66 Roman camps in northern Spain, showing the immensity of the empire's attacks against the Cantabri.
The latest find is helping researchers understand the scale and location of Rome's fight for control of the Iberian Peninsula.
"It is an important step in understanding how the conquest was carried out on the Cantabrian slope of León, an area where it was necessary to link the Roman camps with Iron Age settlements," Carlos Fernández Rodríguez, an archaeologist at the University of León, said in the statement.
Can you identify these historical objects of war? Test your smarts with our weapons of the world quiz!
Kristina Killgrove is a staff writer at Live Science with a focus on archaeology and paleoanthropology news. Her articles have also appeared in venues such as Forbes, Smithsonian, and Mental Floss. Kristina holds a Ph.D. in biological anthropology and an M.A. in classical archaeology from the University of North Carolina, as well as a B.A. in Latin from the University of Virginia, and she was formerly a university professor and researcher. She has received awards from the Society for American Archaeology and the American Anthropological Association for her science writing.

articles.title: Độc lạ loài bò lớn nhất thế giới ở Việt Nam: Nặng tới 2 tấn, mang nguồn gene quý hiếm
articles.text:
Loài bò này mang nhiều đặc tính quý và được coi là một nguồn gene hiếm cần được bảo tồn.
Theo Báo Công an nhân dân, từ những năm 2009 đến đầu năm 2015 tại thôn Bạc Rây 2 (xã Phước Bình, huyện Bác Ái, tỉnh Ninh Thuận) là vùng đệm vườn quốc gia Phước Bình, có một con bò đực thường xuyên xuất hiện mùa mưa tầm tháng 6 đến tháng 9, nhập đàn bò nhà của nông dân và kiếm ăn chung trên cánh đồng cỏ ven rừng. Con bò đực này cao khoảng 1,7m, dài hơn 2m, nặng khoảng 1 tấn.
Con bò đực hoang dã nhập vào đàn bò của người dân được nhận định là loài bò tót Đông Nam Á. (Ảnh: VTC News)
Thân mình con bò màu đen, từng khối cơ nổi lên, bốn chân trắng, nó không có cục u trên lưng như bò nhà mà có hẳn một sống cơ nổi lên chạy dài dọc sống lưng. Nó có cặp sừng to, cong vút, mút sừng nhọn hoắt vươn ra phía trước. Người cho rằng đó là trâu rừng, có ý kiến lại bảo phải là bò hoang mới đúng. Sau đó cán bộ kiểm lâm tới quan sát và nhận dạng thì nó đích thị là bò tót.
Bò tót Đông Nam Á là loài bò mang nhiều đặc tính quý hiếm. (Ảnh: Pixabay).
Theo báo cáo của nhóm chuyên gia tới nghiên cứu, con bò tót đực này thuộc nhóm bò tót Đông Nam Á (Bos gaurus), rất hung dữ. Độ hung hãn chỉ đứng sau loài hổ. Bò tót sẵn sàng tấn công nếu phát hiện nơi ẩn nấp của thợ săn. Chúng luôn phản kháng đến cùng khi cảm thấy bị đe dọa. Là loài thú hung dữ, có vóc dáng khổng lồ nên bò tót hầu như không có thiên địch. Trên đồng cỏ vùng Bạc Rây, bò tót đực trở thành bá chủ và chinh phục đàn bò nhà giống cái.
Loại bò này còn được gọi là bò rừng Mã Lai hay bò rừng bison Ấn Độ, trên thực tế, chúng không hề có quan hệ gần gũi với loài bò rừng bison ở châu Âu và Bắc Mỹ.
Tại Việt Nam, loài bò tót Đông Nam Á được người dân tộc thiểu số gọi là con min. (Ảnh: Pixabay).
Theo VTV, tại Việt Nam, bò tót Đông Nam Á được người dân tộc thiểu số gọi là con min, nghĩa là trâu rừng, do có hình dáng tương tự loài trâu. Nhìn ở đằng trước, chúng giống như trâu và ở phía sau lại giống như bò. Bò tót sống thành đàn từ 2 đến 10 cá thể. Những con bò đực già thường sống đơn độc hoặc hợp với nhau thành từng nhóm nhỏ.
Bộ lông ngắn mềm mượt màu nâu thẫm hoặc đen xám hơi phớt xanh bóng ở lưng. Lông ở bụng dài màu nâu nhạt. Con cái thường có màu hung đỏ. Đuôi dài màu đen.
Loài bò tót này nhìn ở đằng trước, chúng giống như trâu và ở phía sau lại giống như bò. (Ảnh: Pixabay).
Bò tót thích ăn lá non, mầm tre non, cỏ non mới mọc ở nương rẫy hoặc các khu vực giáp ranh với rừng. Bò tót Đông Nam Á được các chuyên gia động vật học trên thế giới công nhận là một loài bò rừng lớn nhất trên thế giới. Một con bò đực trưởng thành có thể cao trên 2 mét và nặng tới 2 tấn, to lớn hơn cả trâu rừng châu Á và bò rừng ở Bắc Mỹ. Với kích thước này, bò tót là loài thú lớn thứ 3 về chiều cao, chỉ xếp sau loài hươu cao cổ và voi. Chúng là loài có trọng lượng cơ thể đứng thứ 5 trong các loài động vật trên cạn: sau voi, tê giác trắng, tê giác Ấn Độ và hà mã.
Bò tót Đông Nam Á sinh sản thường vào tháng 6, 7. Mỗi năm đẻ 1 lứa, mỗi lứa một con. Bò tót mang thai khoảng 270 ngày, đẻ mỗi năm một lứa, mỗi lứa một con. Nơi sinh sống của bò tót là rừng già thường xanh, rừng khộp, rừng hỗn giao tre nứa, rừng thứ sinh địa hình tương đối bằng ở độ cao 500 - 1500m so với mặt nước biển.
Bò tót Đông Nam Á được các chuyên gia động vật học trên thế giới công nhận là một loài bò rừng lớn nhất trên thế giới. (Ảnh: Pixabay).
Bò tót Đông Nam Á mang nhiều đặc tính quý như tầm vóc lớn, khả năng chống chịu tốt với điều kiện khí hậu khắc nghiệt…, được coi là một nguồn gene quý hiếm cần được bảo tồn và có thể phát triển để phục vụ nhân giống.
Chúng đã được liệt kê là loài dễ bị tổn thương trong sách đỏ IUCN kể từ năm 1986. Số lượng toàn cầu được ước tính tối đa là 21.000 cá thể trưởng thành vào năm 2016. Chúng đã giảm hơn 70% trong ba thế hệ gần đây và có lẽ đã tuyệt chủng ở Sri Lanka và cũng có thể ở Bangladesh. Trong các khu vực được bảo vệ tốt, số lượng chúng ổn định và ngày càng tăng.
Chúng đã được liệt kê là loài bò dễ bị tổn thương trong sách đỏ IUCN kể từ năm 1986. (Ảnh: Pixabay).
Hiện nay, tại Việt Nam chỉ còn khoảng 300 con bò tót, phân bố chủ yếu tại vườn quốc gia Mường Nhé (Điện Biên), vùng rừng núi Tây Nguyên, vườn quốc gia Chư Mom Rây (Kon Tum) và vườn quốc gia Cát Tiên (Lâm Đồng), sân bay Phú Bài (Huế).Tuy nhiên, những đàn bò tót này đang đứng trước hiểm họa diệt chủng cao do rừng bị chặt phá và nạn săn trộm thú quý.
Số lượng của loài bò tót này ngày càng giảm do 2 nguyên nhân chính:
Loài bò tót này đang đứng trước hiểm họa diệt chủng cao do nạn săn trộm để lấy túi mật. (Ảnh: VTC News).
Theo trang VTC News, nhiều người đồn rằng mật bò tót có thể giúp: tráng dương, mạnh gân cốt, bổ khí, tốt cho sinh lý của đàn ông và hỗ trợ chữa nhiều chứng bệnh nan y… Mật bò tót còn được cho là có dược tính cao hơn cả mật rắn hổ chúa hay mật gấu. Tuy nhiên, trên thực tế, các chuyên gia đã chứng minh rằng mật bò tót không khác gì mật trâu, bò.
Hơn nữa, trong cơ thể người, mật chỉ tiết ra một lượng nhỏ vừa đủ giúp tiêu hóa thức ăn hằng ngày, nếu đưa thêm một lượng mật, dù của động vật nào, vào cơ thể cao hơn mức bình thường đều có nguy cơ gây ngộ độc. Chưa kể nếu uống phải mật động vật bị bệnh (nhiễm khuẩn, thương hàn, bệnh do sán lá Fasciola gigantica ký sinh trong gan và ống dẫn mật gây ra) thì càng nguy hiểm hơn.

articles.title: Scientists discover how exercise reverses muscle aging
articles.text:
Scientists discover how exercise reverses muscle aging
- Date:
- October 15, 2026
- Source:
- Duke-NUS Medical School
- Summary:
- Scientists have uncovered a hidden biological mechanism that helps explain how exercise can reverse some of the damage caused by muscle aging. The key is a gene called DEAF1, which becomes overactive with age and interferes with the muscles’ ability to clear damaged proteins and repair themselves. Exercise can help restore this balance, allowing older muscles to rebuild and regain strength, although the benefits may diminish when the system becomes too disrupted.
- Share:
Scientists have uncovered a biological mechanism that helps explain how exercise protects aging muscles and restores their ability to repair themselves. The discovery reveals why physical activity can counteract some of the changes that weaken muscles with age and points toward potential new treatments for age-related muscle loss.
The research, led by Duke-NUS Medical School in collaboration with Singapore General Hospital and Cardiff University, identified a molecular system that becomes disrupted as muscles grow older. Exercise can help bring this system back into balance, allowing muscle cells to remove damaged proteins and maintain healthy tissue.
Published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS), the findings provide new insight into the biology of muscle aging. They also help explain why exercise may be more effective for some older individuals than others.
Although the experiments were conducted in fruit flies and mice, the researchers believe the underlying mechanism could eventually help scientists develop new approaches to preserving muscle strength and mobility in humans.
Why Muscles Become Weaker With Age
Muscle loss is one of the most significant physical changes associated with aging. Beginning around midlife, muscles gradually lose strength and function, making everyday activities more difficult and increasing the likelihood of falls and broken bones.
Weaker muscles can also complicate recovery from injuries and illnesses and make it harder for the body to regulate blood sugar. Because muscles play an important role in metabolism, their deterioration can affect far more than physical strength.
For aging populations, including Singapore's, maintaining muscle health is especially important. Preventing muscle decline can help older adults remain independent while reducing the demands placed on caregivers and healthcare systems.
At the cellular level, keeping muscles healthy requires a careful balance between producing new proteins and disposing of old or damaged ones. Proteins form much of the machinery and structure within muscle cells, so this ongoing maintenance is essential for normal function.
One of the main systems responsible for regulating this process is a signaling pathway called mTORC1. It acts as a growth regulator, helping cells determine when to manufacture proteins and support muscle maintenance.
However, this system can become less balanced with age.
When mTORC1 becomes excessively active, muscle cells may devote too much attention to producing proteins while failing to clear away damaged ones. Over time, these defective proteins accumulate, placing stress on cells and interfering with their ability to function properly.
Scientists have long recognized this imbalance as a contributor to muscle deterioration, but the mechanism responsible for pushing the system out of balance remained unclear.
Scientists Discover a Key Gene Behind Muscle Aging
The researchers traced the problem to a gene called DEAF1, which appears to play an important role in controlling how muscles age.
As muscles grow older, DEAF1 levels can increase. The team discovered that this rise drives excessive mTORC1 activity, disrupting the normal cycle of protein production and removal.
The result is a breakdown in muscle maintenance. Instead of efficiently replacing damaged components and preserving healthy tissue, aging muscle cells become increasingly burdened by proteins that should have been cleared away.
Under normal circumstances, DEAF1 is regulated by a family of proteins known as FOXOs.
These proteins help control gene activity and are involved in important cellular maintenance processes. In healthy muscles, they prevent DEAF1 from becoming excessively active.
But FOXO activity tends to decline with age. As this protective regulation weakens, DEAF1 can increase, driving mTORC1 activity higher and further disrupting the processes needed to maintain muscle health.
The researchers found that this chain of events helps explain why aging muscles gradually lose their capacity to repair themselves.
Crucially, they also discovered that exercise can interrupt the process.
How Exercise Helps Aging Muscles Repair Themselves
Exercise does more than stimulate muscles to grow stronger. According to the findings, physical activity can also help restore the cellular maintenance system that becomes disrupted during aging.
The researchers found that exercise activates regulatory proteins that reduce DEAF1 levels. This helps return mTORC1 activity to a healthier balance, allowing muscle cells to remove damaged proteins while continuing to produce the new proteins they need.
In effect, exercise helps muscles perform an important internal cleanup, making it easier for them to maintain healthy tissue and recover from damage.
Assistant Professor Tang Hong-Wen, the study's lead author from the Cancer and Stem Cell Biology Program at Duke-NUS, explained:
"Exercise can reverse this process, correcting the imbalance. Physical activity activates certain proteins which lower DEAF1 levels, bringing the growth pathway back into balance. This allows aging muscles to clear out damaged proteins, rebuild themselves properly, and help them stay stronger and more resilient."
However, the researchers discovered an important limitation.
When DEAF1 levels become extremely elevated or FOXO activity falls too low, exercise may no longer be sufficient to fully restore normal muscle repair.
This suggests that the biological condition of muscle cells can influence how effectively they respond to physical activity. It also offers a possible explanation for why some older adults experience greater improvements from exercise than others.
The findings do not suggest that exercise loses its value with age. Rather, they indicate that understanding the biological changes occurring inside aging muscles may be necessary to develop more effective strategies for preventing muscle decline.
Experiments Reveal a Way to Restore Muscle Strength
To investigate the role of DEAF1, the researchers performed experiments using fruit flies and older mice.
These two animal models allowed the team to examine whether the same biological mechanism influences muscle health across very different species.
The results revealed a consistent pattern.
When the researchers increased DEAF1 levels, muscles weakened rapidly. But when they reduced DEAF1, the balance between protein production and removal improved, and muscle strength was restored.
Finding similar effects in both fruit flies and mice suggests that DEAF1 participates in an evolutionarily conserved system, meaning the underlying biological function has been maintained across species over long periods of evolution.
These experiments also provided evidence that DEAF1 is not simply associated with muscle deterioration. Changing its levels directly affected muscle function, strengthening the case that it plays an important role in the aging process.
Whether targeting this system can produce comparable benefits in humans remains to be established.
Could Scientists Mimic the Benefits of Exercise?
The implications of the discovery may extend beyond ordinary muscle aging.
DEAF1 also influences muscle stem cells, which are specialized cells that help repair and regenerate muscle tissue after injury or damage.
As people age, these cells become less effective, and their numbers or activity can decline, making recovery more difficult. Disruptions involving DEAF1 may further impair the body's ability to regenerate healthy muscle.
By identifying DEAF1 as an important regulator, researchers have uncovered a potential target for therapies designed to improve muscle maintenance and recovery.
Such treatments could eventually benefit people who have difficulty exercising, including those recovering from major surgery, serious illness, or chronic conditions such as cancer.
One possibility is that adjusting DEAF1 activity could reproduce some of the molecular changes normally triggered by physical activity. This might help preserve muscle strength even when a person's ability to exercise is limited.
However, this remains a potential future application rather than an established treatment. Further research will be needed to determine whether manipulating DEAF1 is both safe and effective in humans.
Priscillia Choy Sze Mun, the study's first author and a research assistant in the Cancer and Stem Cell Biology Program at Duke-NUS, described the discovery:
"Exercise tells muscles to 'clean up and reset.' Lowering DEAF1 helps older muscles regain strength and balance, almost like hitting the rewind button. With millions of older adults at risk of muscle decline, understanding DEAF1 could lead to new ways to protect muscles and improve quality of life."
A New Direction for Fighting Age-Related Muscle Loss
The findings highlight an important distinction between simply stimulating muscle growth and maintaining the cellular systems that keep muscles healthy.
Producing more proteins is not always beneficial if damaged proteins are allowed to accumulate. Effective muscle maintenance requires both processes to work together.
By showing how exercise helps restore this balance, the researchers have identified a potential biological explanation for some of its protective effects against muscle aging.
Professor Patrick Tan, Senior Vice-Dean for Research at Duke-NUS, emphasized the broader significance:
"This study helps explain, at a molecular level, why aging muscles lose their ability to repair themselves and why exercise can restore that balance in some individuals. By identifying DEAF1 as a key regulator in this process, these findings may lead to new ways in which the benefits of exercise can be brought to societies with rapidly aging populations."
The discovery may ultimately help researchers design interventions that complement physical activity, particularly for people whose muscles no longer respond as effectively to exercise.
For now, the research reinforces the importance of exercise while revealing that its benefits depend on an intricate network of molecular processes inside muscle cells.
As populations around the world grow older, understanding these processes could become increasingly valuable for protecting mobility, supporting recovery, and helping people maintain their independence later in life.

articles.title: 'Birdman' copper plate: A 700-year-old depiction of a Native American warrior that may be a woman holding a weapon and a severed head
articles.text:
'Birdman' copper plate: A 700-year-old depiction of a Native American warrior that may be a woman holding a weapon and a severed head
Discovered in an Indigenous grave in Georgia nearly 150 years ago, the "Birdman" copper plate may actually depict a woman ceremonially dressed as a warrior.
QUICK FACTS
Name: "Birdman" copper plate
What it is: A copper plate with a hammered decoration
Where it is from: Cahokia Mounds, Illinois
When it was made: 13th century
This copper plate was discovered in the late 19th century in a prehistoric Native American burial at the Etowah Indian Mounds archaeological site in Georgia, but it was likely made hundreds of miles away at Cahokia Mounds in Illinois. While the decorative plate showcases long-distance trade and a shared ritual culture among early Indigenous groups in the southeastern United States, the nature of the human figure depicted on the artifact has been debated for over a century.
The "Birdman" relic is one of two hammered copper plates that Smithsonian archaeologist John P. Rogan unearthed in the 1880s while digging in a burial mound at Etowah, a centuries-old village occupied by thousands of Native Americans from 1000 to 1550. Etowah was part of the "mound-building," or Mississippian, phase of Indigenous occupation; other famous sites include Moundville in Alabama and Cahokia in Illinois. These groups had extensive trade networks and shared a common artistic and ceremonial tradition known as the Southeastern Ceremonial Complex.
This copper artifact, known as Rogan Plate 1 or the "Birdman" plate, is in the collection of the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History in Washington, D.C. The plate is roughly 11 inches (28 centimeters) tall and had been buried with a high-status person who likely died at Etowah in the mid-14th century. But experts believe the copper plate was an heirloom made decades earlier, at Cahokia, and traded south to Etowah.
A human figure dominates the copper plate with its elaborate bird costume. The person carries a severed head by the hair in their left hand, while their right hand holds a club or mace. The figure also wears a pleated skirt or loincloth that may have been made from human scalps. This bird-human figure is commonly depicted in the Southeastern Ceremonial Complex and has been called a dancing warrior, eagle warrior, eagle dancer, hawk dancer, falcon dancer and falcon warrior. But more often, the figure is called Birdman or Morning Star, a prehistoric Mississippian hero associated with agriculture and rebirth.
Archaeologists' interpretations of the Birdman plaque from Etowah have long assumed that the represented figure is a male warrior. In a 2004 study, for example, archaeologist Adam King wrote that "this plaque would have served as an emblem of office awarded to a chieftain, and would have accompanied him as a sign of his strength among the ancestral spirits."
But the sex of the skeleton in the Etowah burial is unclear, and there were high-status graves of both men and women at Etowah, archaeologist Billie Follensbee and art historian Katie Buford wrote in a 2017 study. Although experts previously assumed that both Rogan Plate 1 and Rogan Plate 2 represented male warriors, Follensbee and Buford found that the figures have slender bodies with prominent right breasts, suggesting the "Birdman" may have actually been female.
"A female bird-human warrior could have represented a gender variant individual in the form of the well-known Native American phenomenon of the 'manly-hearted woman,' a woman who has assumed the usually male role and the garb of a combat soldier," Follensbee and Buford wrote. In addition to the historic term "manly-hearted woman," third-gender or gender-variant individuals in Indigenous North America are often referred to as "two-spirit," a broad term Indigenous people coined in 1990 to describe people who take on gender-nonconforming roles.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
The commemoration of a two-spirit individual on a copper artifact, as well as the use of the artifact as a high-status grave good, "not only demonstrates the Native American cultural acceptance of such gender variant roles but also further serves to celebrate the elite status and achievements of these 'manly-hearted women,'" Follensbee and Buford wrote.
For more stunning archaeological discoveries, check out our Astonishing Artifacts archives.
Can you put together last week's Astonishing Artifact?
Kristina Killgrove is a staff writer at Live Science with a focus on archaeology and paleoanthropology news. Her articles have also appeared in venues such as Forbes, Smithsonian, and Mental Floss. Kristina holds a Ph.D. in biological anthropology and an M.A. in classical archaeology from the University of North Carolina, as well as a B.A. in Latin from the University of Virginia, and she was formerly a university professor and researcher. She has received awards from the Society for American Archaeology and the American Anthropological Association for her science writing.
