articles.title: Jim Cramer says the recent AI stock sell-off echoes a crucial lesson from the 1987 market crash
articles.text:
CNBC’s Jim Cramer said the 1987 market crash offers an important lesson that can be applied to the recent AI stock sell-off.
Monday marked 39 years since Black Monday, when the Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged 22.6% in a single session. The historic crash was fueled in part by portfolio insurance strategies designed to protect investors against losses. Instead, they triggered waves of automatic selling that sent stocks plummeting.
"Rampant, automatic selling destroyed stocks, even as the underlying companies were quite strong," the "Mad Money" host recalled. "In retrospect, it was a spectacular buying opportunity."
Cramer sees echoes of that disconnect in the current AI trade.
The S&P 500 fell nearly 2% last week, its biggest weekly decline since late June, while the Nasdaq Composite tumbled 4.5%, snapping a four-week winning streak. Semiconductor and data center stocks were particularly hard hit, with many falling together despite no apparent deterioration in company fundamentals.
"One of the things I try to teach on this show is how much stocks can diverge from the underlying value of the companies," Cramer said.
Cramer suspects Friday's sell-off may have been intensified by a hedge fund liquidation, similar to the collapse of highly leveraged fund Situational Awareness earlier this summer. While another liquidation has not been confirmed, such events can force funds to unload stocks to cover losses, dragging down shares regardless of whether the companies are in trouble.
"I think we're seeing the same thing right now — stocks having little to nothing to do with the fundamentals — in some, but not all, of the data center stocks," he said. "They all go up in bunches, even if they shouldn't — at least not this fast. And when they go down, they go down in unison, with nothing happening at the companies, just like '87."
For investors, the lesson is to distinguish between a stock falling because its business is weakening and one declining because of forces beyond the company's control.
"On the anniversary of the great crash, remember on this Green Monday that you may be seeing huge moves based on the machinations of money managers, who are out over their skis, or crushing the slalom, all totally divorced from the fundamentals, without a shred of alimony," Cramer concluded.
He called it "Green Monday" because the S&P 500 and Nasdaq made back some of their Friday losses in the first trading day of the week.

Dow Jones Industrial Average futures traded 56 points higher, or 0.1%. S&P 500 futures climbed 0.1%, while Nasdaq-100 futures advanced 0.2%.

In Asia, Japan's Nikkei 225 declined 0.82% in early Tuesday trade, while South Korea's Kospi lost 2.31%. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 traded 0.84% lower.
Tech last week suffered a rout that spilled over into the broader market, as concerns grew around companies borrowing too much money for their artificial intelligence build-outs.
"Improving moods regarding the prospects of modern technology have Wall Street breathing a sigh of relief as participants drop hedges, after the cost of volatility protection soared intraday on Friday, ahead of the intensifying selloff," wrote Jose Torres, senior economist at Interactive Brokers.
CoreWeave, which fell more than 25% last week, tried to recover some of that decline after a Goldman Sachs upgrade to buy. However, early gains fizzled and the stock closed slightly lower.

articles.title: Stock investors are ready to move on from the AI rout. Credit investors are not
articles.text:
AI stocks rallied on Monday, but CoreWeave closed slightly lower as investors remained skittish about its debt. Yields on Oracle debt also remained elevated as credit worries persist across the AI trade.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite gained 1% on Monday. Oracle rose 1% after dropping 9% last week, while Intel climbed 2.4%, Advanced Micro Devices added 1.8% and Micron Technology rose 3%.
CoreWeave, the so-called neocloud company that led the sell-off last week, bounced around, hit a 52-week low and ultimately closed fractionally lower. Meanwhile, its bond yields remained high and its five-year credit default swaps were at distressed levels.
The yield to maturity on its 9.625% bond due in 2032 was at 14.9%, slightly down from its high of over 15% last week. The spread on its five-year credit default swaps stood at roughly 1,082 basis points, nearly 2% lower than Friday.
Credit default swaps are contracts where buyers pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. A spread above 1,000 basis points is generally a sign of distress.
"The market tends to get worried about companies that have refinance risk when rates are higher, and CoreWeave was a little bit of the poster child," said John Lloyd, global head of multi-sector and corporate credit at Janus Henderson. His firm's multi-sector income fund owns CoreWeave 2031 bonds. "They need the debt markets in order to grow, in some form or fashion."
The concern wasn't limited to CoreWeave's bonds. It was also seen in Oracle, which is an investment-grade hyperscaler and considered a bellwether on AI credit. Its five-year CDS spread also moved wider on Monday to 315 basis points, a 311% increase from a year prior.
What's notable is the dispersion in AI-related high-yield bonds, similar to what is happening in the broader junk market, Goldman Sachs said last week.
Neoclouds and firms with significant frontier lab exposure are largely at the epicenter of the funding cost debate, while AI-adjacent energy and utilities have been more resilient since they have more diversified revenue streams and a relatively defensive earnings profile, Amanda Lynam, Goldman's chief credit strategist, said in a note. Investment-grade bonds have also seen less severe price action, she added.
"As the pace of issuance has increased, differentiation factors around construction risk, coverage of principal or refinancing risk, and claim to tenant have become increasingly important," Lynam wrote. "Additional considerations around power availability, permitting, and insurance all advocate for a bottom-up approach to investing in the asset class."
Economist David Rosenberg, founder and president of Rosenberg Research, called Oracle the "canary in the coal mine." Oracle, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta have issued more than $228 billion of bonds this year and now account for about 10% of the global investment-grade market, he noted.
Oracle, which has about $132 billion of net debt and a BBB- rating from S&P Credit Ratings, "is the bridge between junk-rated neoclouds and investment-grade hyperscalers," said Rosenberg, who has a reputation for bearish calls.
"A downgrade to junk would be the clearest sign of contagion."

articles.title: Tech stocks had a nice oversold bounce on Monday. Earnings this week will determine if it's for real
articles.text:
This week's major earnings hold the key to whether this technology comeback has legs, investors said.
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite rallied Monday, largely due to a rebound in artificial intelligence companies. Chip stocks surged, with the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) on pace to snap a nine-day slump. The Magnificent Seven outperformed, as did memory chip makers. The iShares MSCI South Korea ETF (EWY), dominated by SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, surged 4% after also suffering steep declines over the past week.
That comes after the S&P 500 fell nearly 2% last week, its worst weekly decline since late June. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 4.5% over the same five-day span.
Monday looked like a bounce from oversold conditions, but a bigger move will depend on this week's big tech earnings — which include results from major names such as Meta Platforms and Tesla — to clear some of the recent worries about the sustainability of the AI trade. SpaceX reports after the bell Tuesday.
"Tech earnings are key this week. Fundamentals are unchanged, but given fragile price action, we turn neutral [on] risk assets and stay neutral duration," wrote Ajay Rajadhyaksha, global chairman of research at Barclays.
This week will be especially crucial for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, which need to hold support so as not to confirm a further breakdown, Katie Stockton, founder of Fairlead Strategies, said in a Monday note. For the time being, however, widespread, short-term oversold conditions suggest support can hold, she said.
Earnings test
Of the 47 S&P 500 companies that have reported their third quarter thus far, 85% have beaten expectations, and the broad market index is on track to post a blended earnings growth rate of 29%.
But the bulk of tech results are still to come, and they have a high bar to clear.
"Investors are going to need proof statements from any company that is considered part of the AI trade that they can deliver on the earnings growth expectations being built into their pricing," said Ron Albahary, chief investment officer at LNW. "We don't have a valuation-potential bubble here like we had in the internet bubble. We have an earnings-expectation-potential bubble in this cycle."
As a result, the market will take a "more discriminating" approach to tech, which Albahary views as a healthy move that will lead to "more of a dispersion of winners and losers within the AI trade universe." In that environment, some AI beneficiaries may continue to rise, while others like the neocloud platforms may sell off due to the amount of debt they're taking on to finance the build-out, he said.
"Previously, the AI headlines would drive the bulk of the AI universe stocks up or down," the CIO said. "I don't think we're going to see that kind of uniformity going forward."
As it stands now, action in the AI trade appears to be more of a "reality check" than a "full-blown unraveling," according to Wells Fargo Investment Institute's Sameer Samana. But he still believes there may be more pressure in the days and maybe even weeks ahead.
"We recently downgrade[d] tech because we thought expectations had gotten too optimistic, and while the recent selling has taken some of that optimism out of the equation, we don't think it's fully done and may last through the midterms given the politicization of AI/data centers," the Wells Fargo head of global equities and real assets told CNBC.

articles.title: Trump says he'd meet with Putin and Xi, criticizes Zelenskyy
articles.text:
President Donald Trump said Monday that he would meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping to discuss how to end the Ukraine war, while ramping up his criticism of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
Trump suggested that a meeting between the world leaders, which Putin reportedly proposed, could take place without Zelenskyy present.
"Anything I can do to end the war, whether somebody's there or not," Trump told reporters when asked about the potential meeting as he departed the White House for a campaign rally in Kansas.
The comments came as tensions between Trump and Zelenskyy have steadily risen in recent weeks, while Russia — which invaded Ukraine in 2022 — has received multiple breaks from the U.S.
Trump had initially suggested that he would be more interested in discussing "denuclearization" with Putin and Xi, saying, "Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine. They haven't been doing much."
The Wall Street Journal had reported that Putin in an Oct. 9 phone call with Trump floated the idea of a trilateral summit with Xi next month.
That meeting could take place at the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, which is set for Nov. 18 and Nov. 19, the Journal reported.
"If President Xi wants to have it, I'd have it. I'm sure we'd talk about other things like trade too. But yeah, I would do that," Trump said in Monday's remarks.
He also said that Russia and China, which have both been accused of supporting Iran in its ongoing military efforts against the U.S., have done "very little" for Tehran.
And when asked about Zelenskyy's criticism of Trump's recent decision to waive new sanctions against Russia — and his recent claim that Trump is on the wrong side of history — the U.S. president once again lashed out at the Ukrainian leader.
"Zelenskyy doesn't know what he's talking about," Trump said. "Zelenskyy is a man that should have had this war settled a long time ago."
"I think it's time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine," Trump added, echoing his prior call for Kyiv to "get a new president."
Zelenskyy says that Starlink and Starshield, the critical satellite services offered by Elon Musk's SpaceX, have recently been degraded, and that U.S. intelligence sharing has also been disrupted, leaving Ukraine without advance warning of Russian strikes.
"No explanation for either of these issues has been provided to Ukraine by the American side," Zelenskyy said earlier Monday after a call with bipartisan U.S. lawmakers from the House and Senate.
Trump said outside the White House that he does not know who ordered the interruption to the Starlink service, "But I'd like to find out."
Musk said last week that the U.S. government and Trump are "ultimately" responsible for any slowdowns. But Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied that the U.S. caused the interruption, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned Zelenskyy to be "very careful about making statements like this that aren't true."
Zelenskyy also once again criticized Trump's decision to waive key provisions of a new Russian sanctions bill, which was signed last month after passing Congress with broad bipartisan support.
He said he showed the lawmakers photos from the scene of a Russian attack in the Kharkiv region that killed six people, including a mother and her 1-year-old child.
"This is how Russia responds to the lifting of sanctions and the easing of pressure," Zelenskyy said.
Sens. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., and Thom Tillis, R-N.C., said in a joint statement after the meeting, "Funding Russia's war machine, disabling Ukraine's satellite communications, and crippling its air defense are all impediments to peace."
"Trying to appease a murderous thug like Vladimir Putin will only prolong this war and bring greater casualties," the senators said.
Trump had already been criticized by members of both parties after announcing a deal allowing Russia to supply diesel fuel on the global market, despite existing sanctions.
But in Monday's remarks, Trump pushed back, saying he is "not looking to break up negotiations" with Putin on deals pertaining to Ukraine, Iran, diesel and the release of hostages.

articles.title: Crushed tech stocks bounce — plus, new doctor survey keeps us positive on Lilly
articles.text: Every weekday, the CNBC Investing Club with Jim Cramer releases the Homestretch — an actionable afternoon update, just in time for the last hour of trading on Wall Street. Stocks are higher on Monday as investors assess last week's tech carnage and buy the pullbacks in chip stocks. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) is on pace to snap a nine-session losing streak — set to end its worst stretch since May 2006. The Nasdaq is up 1%. However, we would characterize the bounce as tepid. The SOXX is trading well off its best levels of the session, and market focal point CoreWeave has flipped from positive to negative on the day. The stock is making a new low for the year under $60 per share. Still, as money rotated into semiconductor stocks , it moved out of defensive groups that rallied last week, including healthcare and consumer staples. That's why the Dow is near flat. Oil is on the move, with WTI crude increasing about $2 to around $103 per barrel. Rising oil prices are fueling inflation concerns and leading to a selloff in bonds, with the yield on the 10-year Treasury up on the day. The uptick comes after a week in which yields significantly pulled back as part of a flight to safety in the market. Remember, when bond prices go up from investor buying yield go down. The opposite is also true as bond prices and yields move inversely to one and othter. The market for obesity drugs is getting bigger thanks to the introduction of daily pills and Medicare coverage this year, keeping the wind at Eli Lilly's back. That's the conclusion of Bank of America analysts following their third-quarter physician survey. In a note to clients Monday, they raised their price target on Lilly shares to $1,397 apiece from $1,341. While the stock is slightly lower Monday, it has had a nice move this month and sits about 2% below its record close set on Aug. 19. To be sure, the notion that pills and Medicare's temporary Bridge access program are meaningfully growing the GLP-1 market isn't new — Lilly CEO David Ricks made this case in a September CNBC interview. But given the potential for there to be some cannibalization of existing patients, it's encouraging to get additional evidence supporting the mostly expansionary view. Lilly's oral Foundayo launched in the U.S. in April, about three months after main rival Novo Nordisk introduced its Wegovy pill. Medicare coverage began July 1. "Our 3Q physician obesity survey adds validation for oral GLP-1s and the Medicare Bridge as US category expanders, with both deriving ~70% of volumes from patients new to GLP-1s (naïve or restarts)," BofA analysts wrote. Also encouraging is that respondents to BofA's survey expect Foundayo to "keep gaining share over the next 12 months" relative to the Wegovy pill. In the U.S., analysts wrote that "Foundayo is now at 27% of oral GLP-1 new starts, and our survey indicates 40% share by 2028/29." Novo's Wegovy pill is proving to be a more formidable competitor than perhaps we expected given its food-and-water restrictions. But, at this point, what we want to see is Lilly's continued progress in closing the gap. Lilly reports Q3 earnings Oct. 29. Up next on the earnings calendar : Steel Dynamics, Crown Holdings, and a couple of regional banks in Western Alliance and Zions report after the bell. It's a big industrial earnings day on Tuesday morning with GE Aerospace, RTX, 3M, and General Motors scheduled to report. On the data side Tuesday morning, it's data on housing starts and building permits, and pending home sales. On Tuesday evening, Club name Capital One reports earnings, followed the next night by fellow portfolio holding Meta Platforms . articles.title: Wells Fargo's comeback is just getting started. Here's why I'm buying
articles.text: I like to invest in quality companies that have fallen out of favor but have a catalyst that could turn things around. That's exactly what I see in Wells Fargo . After moving past years of regulatory restrictions, we're finally starting to see the benefits. The San Francisco-based bank is one of the country's largest lenders, offering everything from consumer checking accounts and credit cards to mortgages and business loans. Key points The lifting of Wells Fargo's asset cap gives the bank room to invest, expand lending and win market share. Third-quarter average loan growth of 11% suggests the bank's growth strategy is starting to pay off. Improving net interest income and margins are encouraging signs that profitability can continue to strengthen. The sixth biggest U.S. bank just reported generally solid earnings, with improving net interest income and margins, resilient consumer activity and stable credit quality. But Wells Fargo stands out to me because its turnaround still appears to be gaining momentum. Why I'm buying The bank can finally focus on growth For seven years, Wells Fargo operated under a Federal Reserve-imposed asset cap that limited its total assets to roughly $1.95 trillion. The restriction was lifted on June 3, 2025 , marking a major turning point for the bank. This is a big deal. With the cap in place, Wells Fargo couldn't expand its balance sheet the way other major banks could, making it harder to compete for new business and grow market share. Now management has more freedom to invest in the business, make loans and pursue opportunities that were previously out of reach. Loan growth is picking up I was encouraged by Wells Fargo's third-quarter results. Average loans grew 11% year over year, driven by growth in commercial and industrial lending, credit cards and auto loans. To me, that's some of the clearest evidence yet that the bank is taking advantage of its newfound flexibility. WFC YTD mountain Wells Fargo, YTD Lending profitability is improving Loan growth alone isn't enough. I also want to see Wells Fargo making more money from its lending business. Third-quarter net interest income, or the difference between interest earned and interest paid, rose 5% year over year to $12.5 billion. The bank also maintained its full-year outlook of approximately $50 billion . Wells Fargo reported a return on tangible common equity of 16.3% in the quarter. I believe the bank can eventually reach 17% to 18%, leaving room for further improvement in profitability. Why now? Despite signs of progress, Wells Fargo shares are trading around $83, roughly 15% below their 52-week high. At about 10.9 times earnings and 1.5 times book value, I see quality on sale. As the bank's turnaround gains momentum, I believe the stock has room to catch up with its peers. Bottom line I give CEO Charlie Scharf a lot of credit for steering Wells Fargo through years of regulatory challenges and putting the bank back on a path to growth. Under his leadership, Wells Fargo is finally shifting from defense to offense, and I believe the best of its turnaround is still ahead. Stephanie Link is the Chief Investment Strategist at Hightower Advisors, where her division manages $8.5 billion in assets (as of June 4, 2026). She has 35 years of experience managing money and serves on KKR's investment council. She earned a B.S. in finance from Boston College. Disclosures: Link owns in Hightower Advisors. articles.title: Apple's iPhone Duo is proving itself the catalyst that Jim Cramer said it would be
articles.text: Apple's iPhone Duo is shaping up to be the new growth engine that Jim Cramer predicted it would be. In the days leading up to Duo preorders this past Friday, Jim said many times that Apple's first foldable device would be a blockbuster. He also called out investors for selling off shares. So far, early indications suggest very strong demand for the Duo. As of Monday morning, the Club's check of Apple's website showed that the earliest estimated delivery date for a Night Sky-colored Duo with 512GB of storage is Jan. 25, or more than three months away. The phone becomes available in stores this coming Friday. This early demand is an encouraging signal for Jim, who has been impressed with the Duo since previewing it last month at Apple's flagship store in New York and can't wait to buy one. "When I played with it, I was blown away, and all I could think about was watching the NFL Sunday Ticket on my Duo," Jim said Monday. "This screen is revolutionary — no seam. The form factor is perfect for watching." Wall Street has taken notice, too. Morgan Stanley reported late Friday that the global 14-week average preorder lead time was a record. "[It is] the longest of any iPhone model we've tracked in the last 10 years," analysts wrote in a note to clients. According to the analysts, the milestone highlights both early demand and limited supply. By contrast, lead times for the iPhone 18 Pro models are lower year over year, according to Morgan Stanley. As Club portfolio director Jeff Marks pointed out Friday, it is a good sign that the Duo has gotten off to a rip-roaring start because, as Morgan Stanley analysts noted, the 18 is not as strong. Jeff said, "Remember, the reason why the 18 may not be as robust is because people have been waiting for the Duo." Melius Research followed up Monday, citing the Duo as one of several reasons that Apple's rally to a $5 trillion valuation can continue. The stock closed above that threshold for the first time last Wednesday, making it the second U.S. company to do so. Fellow Club name Nvidia was the first. Jim has "own them, don't trade them" designations on both. "We have held this thing [the Duo] and used it — and see a hit here long-term, especially as the camera keeps improving in future models," Melius analyst Ben Reitzes wrote in a Monday note to clients. Reitzes and his team estimate that Apple could sell at least 15 million Duo units at average selling prices ranging between $2,000 and $3,200 in fiscal year 2027, generating approximately $40 billion in revenue, with at least half of that number being incremental. Reitzes added, "Heck, the near-term [Duo] shortage may help the sales of iPhone 18 Pros and Max models even." Beyond the Duo, Melius also sees an opportunity for Apple to benefit from higher selling prices across its broader iPhone lineup. "We see a path toward closer to 20% iPhone revenue growth as shortages alleviate, which could add roughly [50 cents] to Apple's earnings per share [for fiscal 2027] and keep the multiple right where it is, if not higher." Reitzes noted that his forecast is roughly double Wall Street's consensus of iPhone revenue growth of 10% in fiscal 2027. Melius maintained a buy rating and $370 price target, but said this "has room to go higher coming out of earnings on November 2nd." Apple will be reporting its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter that evening. Investors, like us, will be anxious to hear any commentary about Apple's upcoming holiday quarter, which is the first period of the company's 2027 fiscal year. AAPL YTD mountain Apple YTD After hitting a 52-week low of about $243 per share on Jan. 20, Apple shares have climbed over 41% to current levels around $342 each, which is only slightly below Friday's record-high close. On a year-to-date basis, Apple shares are up nearly 26%. While most of that gain came with ex-CEO Tim Cook at the helm, shares have continued to move higher since John Ternus took over on Sept. 1. The current iPhone rollout was set in motion under Cook, but Ternus was right there as Apple's hardware chief. Ternus also has the benefit of Cook sticking around as executive chairman. articles.title: Apple announces product launch event for Oct. 28. Analysts expect touchscreen laptop
articles.text:
Apple announced a product launch event on Oct. 28, sending invitations on Monday to media and analysts for an "Apple Experience in Los Angeles."
The email says "Pro and tell," suggesting the launch will focus on high-end "Pro" devices with powerful homegrown chips.
Ben Reitzes, an analyst at Melius Research, wrote in a note on Monday that he expects new Macs to be introduced, "including a touchscreen notebook," this fall. He said that for CEO John Ternus, who succeeded Tim Cook last month, the launch cadence marks a "meaningful shift" from what has been two events a year.
It will be Apple's third launch in Ternus' brief tenure, following an event at company headquarters for new iPhones, including the foldable Duo, and a gathering in New York centered around smart home hubs and a new speaker with a screen called HomeView.
Apple updated its Mac Mini and Mac Studio desktops with new chips in August, and refreshed its MacBook Pro in the spring, along with a new low-cost MacBook Neo. But Apple's iMac desktop hasn't been updated since October 2024.
In the most recent quarter, Apple's Mac sales accounted for about 10% of overall revenue, as the company remains heavily reliant on iPhones.
Still, Macs have become one of the strongest parts of Apple's artificial intelligence story, thanks to its chips that can access more memory at higher speeds than other consumer processors. Apple shares are up 26% so far this year, outperforming the S&P 500.
Last week, Apple and Meta teamed up to bring a large open-weight model, developed by Meta, to multiple high-end Mac Studios.
Apple has historically been dismissive of touchscreen laptops, with software chief Craig Federighi explaining in 2018 that the ergonomics would fatigue users.

articles.title: Goldman says play defense with these stocks if you're worried about the AI bull failing
articles.text: Investors worried that the artificial intelligence trade might lose steam should look to health care and consumer staples stocks, according to Goldman Sachs. "After months of intensifying pressure from interest rates, concerns about the rising cost of capital have caused the equity market to downgrade its growth expectations," Goldman analysts led by Ben Snider wrote Friday. "A sharp reduction in investor positioning has amplified equity market moves. During the past two weeks our Cyclicals vs. Defensives pair has declined by 6%, and rates and credit markets have reflected similar pressures." Goldman estimates AI capital spending currently contributes about half of S & P 500 earnings growth, but expects that to diminish as spending growth slows. The bank's defensive playbook comes as rising energy prices and interest rates cloud the economic outlook, with higher financing costs raising questions about the durability of the AI infrastructure buildout. Investors concerned about a weaker outcome, however, "should focus on stocks in defensive industries with 'quality' attributes," especially those that have recently lagged the broad market, Goldman said. Here are several names from that made the Goldman screen: Tyson Foods stands out with an 11% trailing four-quarter free cash flow yield, the highest among the companies on Goldman's screen. Shares of the food and beverage company are down nearly 17% over the past six months, according to FactSet data. Tyson also yields 3.72%. CVS Health also made the cut thanks to its 9% free cash flow yield. Its stock has gained 15% for the year, but has fallen 15% in the past three months. CVS offers a 2.88% yield, FactSet data shows. To be sure, Goldman's base case still calls for continued earnings growth. It sees the possibility of a catch-up trade in beaten-up consumer-facing stocks, fueled by weaker energy prices and falling interest rates that its macroeconomic forecasters anticipate in 2027, which will support household spending.

articles.title: Gartner analyst behind tech rout: AI returns are not yet large enough to justify neocloud build-out
articles.text:
Wall Street research and advisory firm Gartner is standing by its forecast that $3.5 trillion in AI investment could be on the rocks due to profitability concerns among the top AI models.
Gartner's forecast, issued last week, helped send shockwaves through the AI trade. The firm's chief forecaster, John Lovelock, told CNBC Monday that returns are not yet backing up the full scale of investment.
Consolidation and takeovers among AI-dedicated companies known as neoclouds could ensue, due partly to a mismatch in timing, he added.
"At the moment, we have more compute capacity than we have demand, and we have a lot of the tokens and processing power being given away in freemium solutions," he told CNBC. "Everyone in the AI race is running for a last-man standing position. Pretty much every market that Gartner is tracking in our AI race is likely to collapse down to a duopoly."
That duopoly for the main commercial frontier models consists of Anthropic and OpenAI. The computing-power asset base that's being constructed by neoclouds to serve that duopoly requires a degree of cash flow for those businesses that isn't yet scaling in proportion to the investment, Lovelock said.
Neoclouds would not be going out of business en masse, Lovelock reiterated, but could be subject to consolidation, such as takeovers and mergers.
As a result of their profitability analysis, Gartner predicted last week that 80% of neoclouds, which are AI-dedicated computing power providers, could cease functioning as independent companies.
Neoclouds were hit hard last week, helping to pull the rest of the stock market down with them.
CoreWeave dropped 25%; Nebius dropped 25%; and IREN fell 16%. The S&P 500 finished down 2% and the Nasdaq Composite fell 4% for the week ending Oct. 16, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average finished up 0.7% as investors rotated away from technology stocks.
CoreWeave was up about 2% in midday trading on Monday, while Nebius was up 3.3% and IREN was ahead 5.6%.
Analysts for Wolfe said in a Sunday note that the Gartner report likely contributed to the market stress.
"By the end of [Wednesday], the market appeared to already be on edge when a report from Gartner dropped, warning that more than $3.5tn in AI infrastructure spending could be exposed to impairment by 2030, with neocloud providers particularly vulnerable," Stephanie Wolfe at Roth wrote to clients.
Lovelock also said Monday that AI is a technology as opposed to a market, comparing it to table salt that will be sprinkled into existing commercial operations rather than creating an inherently new field in which companies will sell differentiated and competing products.
In their Wednesday report, Gartner researchers found that overall "AI revenue will be insufficient to support profitable returns on all planned AI capital expenditures" between 2027 and 2030.
The finding came as revenue growth for frontier algorithm company Anthropic decelerated, falling from 140% growth in the second quarter to 45% growth in the third.
The quarterly revenue level of $16.8 billion for Anthropic, which many tech analysts view as one of the linchpins of the AI trade, is quite small relative to the more than $5 trillion that hyperscalers are expected to invest through 2030, the pace of which is increasing.
OpenAI annual revenue expectations missed by $20 billion the week before, Roth at Wolfe noted.
Gartner hasn't been alone in warning that investors' math for the AI buildout may be off. Jefferies' global head of equity strategy Chris Wood has been warning about capital destruction in AI since at least September. Famous investor Paul Tudor Jones told CNBC last week that macroeconomic considerations would lead to a challenging year for the stock market in 2027.
"[If] we sum up all the buybacks, M&A, all the positive things that have powered this market so much … say since 2009, if I sum up all those and then I subtract from that the IPOs, secondaries, unlocks, et cetera, then you've got certainly the most negative flow picture since 2009," he said.

articles.title: Cornell sexual assault case has some prospective students rethinking plans, consultants say
articles.text:
As Cornell University faces scrutiny over its handling of sexual assault allegations, some prospective students are reconsidering whether to apply, according to college admissions consultants who spoke with CNBC.
The concerns come just weeks before Cornell's Nov. 1 early-decision deadline, when applicants must decide whether to submit an application under a binding agreement to attend the Ivy League university if admitted.
Amid public outrage over the handling of the 2024 alleged incident and the ensuing Jane Doe lawsuit, some high school seniors have decided to take the school out of consideration, according to Christopher Rim, president and CEO of college consulting firm Command Education.
"I originally had nine students applying to Cornell, four were early — now we have zero applying early," he said.
The lawsuit centers on a civil complaint filed in September by a former student identified as Jane Doe. She alleges that in October 2024 she was sexually assaulted at one of the school's fraternity houses on Cornell's campus in Ithaca, New York.
Jamie Beaton, co-founder and CEO of college consulting firm Crimson Education, also said he is "seeing some Cornell applicants reconsider applying there based on campus safety and culture concerns."
Cornell directed CNBC to Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff's Oct. 13 message. In a statement, the university said it is conducting an independent review, led by former U.S. Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates, to examine long-standing policies and practices. Separately, Cornell suspended all fraternity parties and social events for the remainder of the 2026-27 academic year.
"These conversations, and campus protests, have underscored my deep conviction that we must do better: that the time for meaningful and lasting change at Cornell, and at campuses across the country, is now," Kotlikoff said in the statement.
What comes next is key, Rim said. "It's very important for Cornell to make sure they do the right thing and make actual changes to their policies," he said. "Then they are going to have to convince students and families they are serious about it."
Will Cornell's application numbers change?
Changing course so close to the early-decision deadline can be difficult for applicants who have spent months tailoring their applications to a specific Cornell school, a distinctive part of the university's application process, according to Beaton.
Some applicants "feel psychologically committed," he said, and are "staying the course, and are holding onto hope that the scrutiny on Cornell will force it to make serious reforms to institutional conduct and culture as a result of this."
In some cases, applying early decision can improve an applicant's odds of admission but leaves less time to work on the application or compare options. The regular-decision deadline for Cornell is Jan. 2.
Going forward, "what we expect is that things will be loud in the short term," Beaton said, referring specifically to this application cycle. But he added that there will likely be minimal long-term movement in application volumes or yield, which is the percent of students who choose to enroll after being admitted.
"Scandals at highly selective universities don't move application volumes in a lasting way, since the pull of the brand, the outcomes and the network is too strong," Beaton said.
Cornell is the largest Ivy by undergraduate enrollment. With an acceptance rate under 10%, Cornell most recently admitted 5,776 applicants to the Class of 2030, according to the university's independent student newspaper, The Cornell Daily Sun.

articles.title: Capital One, General Motors are among the stocks reporting this week with momentum. Here are the others
articles.text: Capital One and General Motors are among the companies reporting earnings this week with momentum on their side. A total of 70 S & P 500 companies across a smattering of industries — including tech, consumer goods and airlines — will report earnings this week. Among them, there are a few in which Wall Street analysts have become increasingly bullish of late. CNBC Pro screened FactSet data for S & P 500 companies reporting this week with accelerating earnings momentum. Specifically, we looked for stocks that met the following criteria: Consensus earnings per share estimates from analysts are up at least 35% in the past three and six month periods Have buy ratings from at least 55% of the analysts covering the stock Average price targets that imply upside of 10% or more Following a finance-heavy week of earnings last week with six major banks reporting, Capital One made the list. Its consensus earnings estimate is up more than 65% over the past three months to $5.50 per share, and 63% of analysts covering hold a buy rating on the stock. Morgan Stanley analyst Jeffrey Adelson reiterated his overweight rating of Capital One in his earnings preview, noting the more positive performance expected of the firm compared to other consumer finance names. "Multi-year network and expense synergies bode well for EPS growth in 2027-28 as COF purchase volumes convert to Discover's higher interchange network and marketing synergies could be conservative. Credit will continue to improve as Discover will help shift COF's pro forma loan book mix into less consumer subprime," Adelson wrote. He also noted that confidence in Capital One's credit could continue to improve if CEO Rich Fairbank "continues to emphasize the health of Capital One's consumer in the face of macro headwinds." General Motors also made the list. Despite what's expected to be a tough earnings season for automakers, analysts see 32% upside for GM, according to FactSet. The automaker's consensus earnings estimate is also up over 100% in both the past three month and six month periods. GM 3M mountain GM 3-month chart Emmanuel Rosner of Wolfe Research last week said General Motors "has the clearest path to generate continued earnings growth through 2027+, robust FCF and strong capital returns." He also sees room for a guidance raise for the 2026 fiscal year, and expects that "incremental efficiencies" will offset higher input costs due to inflation. In Wolfe's Autos investor poll, 52% of investors were positive on the stock, the second-highest out of automakers included in the survey. In updates to its pipeline, GM announced earlier this month that it plans to bring hybrid models to the U.S. soon, and CEO Mary Barra told CNBC's Jim Cramer that the company plans to introduce "eyes-off, hands-off" technology by 2028. Momentum extends to the healthcare and hospitality sectors as well, with analysts increasing estimates on Abbott Laboratories and Las Vegas Sands. More than 64% of analysts have a buy rating on Abbott, whose stock is up 17.3% over the past three months through Friday's close despite the MedTech sector lagging the S & P 500 for most of 2026. Initiating coverage of the healthcare technologies giant at overweight earlier this month, Barclays said it expects accelerating revenue growth from ABT over the next two years as lagging business areas like nutrition and diagnostics start mounting a comeback and success in the medical device segment continues, with 10%-11% growth expected from 2027-2029. Marina Bay Sands owner Las Vegas Sands has seen its consensus earnings estimate surge a whopping 360% to 74 cents per share over the past six months despite the stock tumbling 14% in September and 10% in August. With its business concentrated in the Asia-Pacific region in recent years, long term growth in Macao's gaming industry and the economic boom provided by events like Formula 1's Singapore Grand Prix could be giving the stock a lift.

articles.title: Giá vàng miếng, vàng nhẫn trơn sáng 20/10 tại SJC, DOJI, PNJ, Bảo Tín Minh Châu và Bảo Tín Mạnh Hải
articles.text:
Giá vàng miếng, vàng nhẫn trơn sáng 20/10 tại SJC, DOJI, PNJ, Bảo Tín Minh Châu và Bảo Tín Mạnh Hải
Hiện giá bán ra vàng miếng, vàng nhẫn phổ biến trên 143 triệu đồng/lượng.
Đầu giờ sáng ngày 20/10, giá vàng miếng tại các doanh nghiệp lớn như SJC, DOJI, PNJ, Bảo Tín Mạnh Hải được niêm yết ở mức 140,1 – 143,1 triệu đồng/lượng. Bảo Tín Minh Châu áp dụng 138,7 – 143,1 triệu đồng/lượng.
Giá vàng nhẫn phổ biến 138,7 – 139,5 triệu đồng/lượng chiều mua vào và 142,5 – 143 triệu đồng/lượng chiều bán ra.
Trên thị trường quốc tế, giá vàng giao ngay sau khi tăng nhẹ lên 4.180 USD/ounce lại quay đầu giảm, hiện về mức 4.132 USD/ounce.
Theo Kitco news, giá vàng thế giới giảm trong phiên giao dịch ngày thứ Hai (19/10) khi đồng USD mạnh lên và lợi suất trái phiếu kho bạc Mỹ tăng cao. Trong khi đó, nhà đầu tư tiếp tục cân nhắc rủi ro lạm phát dai dẳng và triển vọng chính sách lãi suất của Cục Dự trữ Liên bang Mỹ (Fed).
Đà phục hồi của nhóm cổ phiếu công nghệ trên thị trường chứng khoán Mỹ đã làm suy giảm phần nào nhu cầu nắm giữ vàng như một tài sản trú ẩn an toàn. Tuy nhiên, những bất ổn liên quan đến eo biển Hormuz tiếp tục hạn chế áp lực bán trên thị trường kim loại quý.
Thị trường chứng khoán Bắc Mỹ kết thúc phiên giao dịch đầu tuần với diễn biến trái chiều, trong bối cảnh nhóm cổ phiếu công nghệ phục hồi sau đợt bán tháo mạnh vào tuần trước.
Chỉ số S&P 500 tăng 31,29 điểm, tương đương 0,4%, lên 7.690,73 điểm. Chỉ số Dow Jones Industrial Average giảm 36,38 điểm, tương đương 0,1%, xuống 51.966,03 điểm. Trong khi đó, Nasdaq Composite tăng 290,85 điểm, tương đương 1,1%, lên 26.430,89 điểm và Russell 2000 tăng 6,93 điểm, tương đương 0,3%, lên 2.728,30 điểm.
Cổ phiếu công nghệ và bán dẫn dẫn dắt đà phục hồi khi nhà đầu tư đánh giá lại những lo ngại liên quan đến chi phí huy động vốn và nhu cầu đầu tư lớn cho hạ tầng trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI).
Tại Canada, chỉ số S&P/TSX Composite giảm 247,92 điểm, tương đương 0,7%, xuống 35.928,63 điểm, chủ yếu do áp lực từ nhóm cổ phiếu tài chính và khai thác kim loại.
Trong khi đó, thị trường chứng khoán châu Âu đồng loạt giảm mạnh sau khi các cuộc biểu tình diễn ra tại Pháp và Italy vào cuối tuần làm dấy lên những lo ngại mới về tình hình tài chính công, chi phí vay nợ và sự ổn định chính trị.
Chỉ số Stoxx Europe 600 giảm 0,80%, xuống 639,56 điểm. Tại Pháp, CAC 40 mất 1,11%, xuống 7.868,05 điểm; DAX của Đức giảm 1,18%, xuống 25.319,77 điểm; FTSE 100 của Anh giảm 1,08%, xuống 10.764,69 điểm. Chỉ số FTSE MIB của Italy cũng giảm 1,55%, xuống 49.086,27 điểm.
Lợi suất trái phiếu chính phủ Pháp tăng khi nhà đầu tư yêu cầu mức bù đắp rủi ro cao hơn đối với nợ công của nước này. Đồng thời, sự suy yếu của đồng euro cũng góp phần hỗ trợ đà tăng của đồng USD.
Trên thị trường tài chính quốc tế, tâm điểm chú ý hiện vẫn là sự trái chiều giữa tốc độ tăng trưởng việc làm chậm lại và áp lực lạm phát dai dẳng tại Mỹ.
Theo số liệu tháng 9, chỉ số giá tiêu dùng (CPI) của Mỹ tăng 0,6% so với tháng trước và tăng 3,7% so với cùng kỳ năm ngoái. Trong khi đó, chỉ số giá sản xuất (PPI) tăng 1,3% so với tháng trước và tăng tới 6,3% so với cùng kỳ.
Doanh số bán lẻ tháng 9 tăng 0,8%, cho thấy sức mua của người tiêu dùng Mỹ vẫn tương đối vững vàng, bất chấp chi phí vay vốn duy trì ở mức cao.
Theo định giá trên thị trường hợp đồng tương lai, xác suất Fed tăng lãi suất tại cuộc họp ngày 27–28/10 hiện ở mức khoảng 15%, đồng nghĩa với việc kịch bản giữ nguyên lãi suất vẫn được đánh giá có khả năng xảy ra cao nhất.
Tuy nhiên, xác suất Fed tiếp tục thắt chặt chính sách tiền tệ trong tháng 12 vẫn ở mức gần 90%, phản ánh những lo ngại về tình trạng lạm phát kéo dài.
Lợi suất trái phiếu kho bạc Mỹ kỳ hạn 10 năm tăng lên khoảng 5,135%, đảo ngược một phần đà tăng giá trái phiếu trong tuần trước. Diễn biến này tiếp tục gây sức ép lên vàng, bởi kim loại quý không mang lại lợi suất và thường kém hấp dẫn hơn khi lợi suất trái phiếu tăng.
Tại châu Á, kinh tế Trung Quốc ghi nhận mức tăng trưởng 4,5% trong quý III so với cùng kỳ năm trước, cao hơn mức 4,3% của quý II, nhờ sự hỗ trợ từ hoạt động xuất khẩu. Tuy nhiên, tiêu dùng trong nước và đầu tư bất động sản vẫn yếu, cho thấy những khó khăn đối với nền kinh tế lớn thứ hai thế giới chưa hoàn toàn được giải quyết.
Trong những ngày tới, nhà đầu tư sẽ tiếp tục theo dõi loạt dữ liệu kinh tế quan trọng của Mỹ, bao gồm số liệu nhà khởi công xây dựng và doanh số bán nhà đang chờ hoàn tất giao dịch vào thứ Ba, số đơn xin trợ cấp thất nghiệp hằng tuần vào thứ Năm, cùng các chỉ số PMI sơ bộ và niềm tin tiêu dùng chính thức tháng 10 vào thứ Sáu.
Các dữ liệu này được kỳ vọng sẽ cung cấp thêm tín hiệu về triển vọng chính sách tiền tệ của Fed trước cuộc họp cuối tháng.
Nếu hoạt động kinh tế và thị trường lao động Mỹ suy yếu, lợi suất trái phiếu có thể giảm, qua đó hỗ trợ giá vàng. Ngược lại, nếu nhu cầu tiêu dùng tiếp tục duy trì vững chắc và kỳ vọng lạm phát ở mức cao, khả năng Fed tăng lãi suất trong tháng 12 có thể được củng cố, tạo thêm áp lực lên thị trường kim loại quý.
An ninh tiền tệ

articles.title: Jim Cramer says the rebound in AI chip stocks may have more room to run
articles.text: Every weekday, the CNBC Investing Club with Jim Cramer holds a "Morning Meeting" livestream at 10:20 a.m. ET. Here's a recap of Monday's key moments. 1. Stocks rebounded Monday following Friday's sharp sell-off. Technology stocks led the recovery as investors returned to beaten-down artificial intelligence names. The tech-heavy Nasdaq jumped 1.8% and the S & P 500 gained nearly 1%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was roughly flat as defensive names took a pause. While remaining bullish on the AI trade , Jim Cramer cautioned against chasing the rally, particularly in stocks that have already bounced sharply. Instead, he recommended investing just a quarter of the money investors want to put to work, then waiting for more clarity before deploying the rest. Jim pointed to relatively stable Treasury yields and lower oil prices as supportive factors. But he emphasized that the market remains vulnerable to volatility. 2. Club holding Micron rebounded 4.5% on Monday alongside memory and storage stocks Western Digital and Sandisk , following a brutal week for the AI trade. The iShares Semiconductor ETF , or SOXX, entered the session on a nine-day losing streak, its longest in more than a decade. The SOXX was up 4% on Monday. Despite the recent volatility, Jim said he's confident in Micron's long-term prospects and sees further upside for the group. "I don't think this move is done," he said. 3. Intel stock got an upgrade to hold from sell at JPMorgan , which sees a more balanced risk-reward outlook after the stock's more than 30% decline from its June high. The analysts acknowledged improved execution and competitiveness under CEO Lip-Bu Tan. They stopped short of a buy rating, citing the need for further progress on Intel's data center CPU roadmap, AI computing strategy, and efforts to secure external foundry customers. Jim said the upgrade is an encouraging sign, but Intel still has more to prove. 4. Stocks covered in Monday's rapid fire at the end of the video were: Cleveland-Cliffs , Estee Lauder , GE Aerospace , and Boeing . (Jim Cramer's Charitable Trust is long INTC, MU. articles.title: Tỷ phú Elon Musk tuyên bố tặng cổ phiếu SpaceX cho tất cả trẻ em Mỹ
articles.text:
Tỷ phú Elon Musk tuyên bố tặng cổ phiếu SpaceX cho tất cả trẻ em Mỹ
Tỷ phú Elon Musk cam kết sẽ tặng một cổ phiếu cho mỗi trẻ em tại Mỹ vào năm 2027. Thông báo này được đưa ra chỉ vài giờ sau khi Anthropic - một “ông lớn” khác trong lĩnh vực trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI) - tuyên bố sẽ dành ra một phần cổ phần của mình vì lợi ích công cộng.
“Trong năm tới, tôi sẽ tặng một cổ phiếu SpaceX của mình cho mỗi trẻ em tại Mỹ”, ông Elon Musk viết trên X. “Đây sẽ là khởi đầu cho nhiều đợt tặng quà tiếp theo”.
Hiện chưa rõ ông Elon Musk sẽ tặng cổ phiếu như thế nào, và vị tỷ phú này cũng không đưa ra thông tin chi tiết về kế hoạch quyên góp của mình.
Theo ước tính từ Cục Thống kê Dân số Mỹ, quốc gia này có khoảng 72 triệu trẻ em. Với mức giá 146 USD/cổ phiếu hiện tại, giá trị của khoản quyên góp này sẽ vào khoảng 10,5 tỷ USD.
Bài đăng của ông Elon Musk xuất hiện sau khi Anthropic công bố kế hoạch dành 5% cổ phần của công ty cho một quỹ chuyên thực hiện các hoạt động đóng góp vì “lợi ích công cộng”.
Các cơ quan quản lý trên toàn cầu đã gia tăng yêu cầu kiểm soát AI sau khi những người trong ngành cảnh báo về khả năng xảy ra các kịch bản thảm khốc.
Anthropic - đơn vị phát triển mô hình AI Claude và đang chuẩn bị cho một đợt phát hành cổ phiếu quy mô lớn - thường xuyên bày tỏ lo ngại về những rủi ro xã hội rộng lớn và các mối nguy hiểm tiềm ẩn từ AI. Công ty này cho biết, một phần nguồn vốn từ quỹ cộng đồng sẽ được sử dụng để giải quyết các “tác động đối với thị trường lao động” do công nghệ này gây ra.
Sau thông báo của Anthropic, ông Elon Musk đã phản hồi trên tài khoản X của công ty này, đề xuất rằng họ nên trao cổ phiếu “trực tiếp cho công chúng”.
Thông báo của ông Musk được đưa ra trong bối cảnh chính quyền của Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump đã thiết lập sáng kiến “Tài khoản Trump”, cung cấp 1.000 USD cho mỗi trẻ em Mỹ sinh ra trong giai đoạn từ năm 2025 đến 2028.
Theo Chỉ số Tỷ phú Bloomberg, ông Elon Musk hiện là người giàu nhất thế giới với khối tài sản ròng hơn 900 tỷ USD. Phần lớn tài sản này đến từ cổ phiếu của SpaceX (khoảng 700 tỷ USD), số còn lại đến từ Tesla, Boring và Neuralink.
Vị tỷ phú này vốn thường đưa ra những ý tưởng không bao giờ trở thành hiện thực, hoặc đề xuất các kế hoạch mà sau đó ông lại giải thích rằng đó chỉ là những lời nói đùa. Ông Musk đã ghim bài đăng mới nhất của mình về việc tặng cổ phiếu SpaceX lên đầu trang cá nhân trên nền tảng X.
Tiền phong

articles.title: We're buying more of a beaten-up stock before another overhang is lifted
articles.text: We are buying 35 shares of Boeing at roughly $191.16. Following the trade, Jim Cramer's Charitable Trust will own 620 shares of BA, increasing its weighting in the portfolio to 3% from 2.8%. We're taking some of the cash proceeds from our TJX Companies trim earlier Monday to pick up more Boeing shares ahead of what could be the removal of another overhang. On Friday, Reuters reported the Federal Aviation Administration could approve Boeing's 737 Max 10 as soon as this week. This would be a major milestone because if the 737 Max 10 is certified this month, Boeing will likely begin delivering these jets to customers in 2027. Certification would reduce uncertainty surrounding potential delays and give investors greater confidence in Boeing's ability to generate free cash flow, the most important metric for evaluating the company's financial performance. Some reports suggest about one-third of the company's 737 Max backlog is for long-delayed Max 10 variant, explaining why this certification is such an important catalyst. The Max 10 is the largest variant in the best-selling 737 Max family and the only version not yet to be approved by the FAA. The regulator approved the smallest member of the family, the Max 7, in August . Boeing has received a series of good news over the past few weeks, including averting a strike with its white-collar union, winning a multi-billion contract with the U.S. Navy, and the FAA ruling that a Max software glitch was not a flight-safety risk , which allowed the Max 10 certification process to continue on its prior timeline. And yet, the stock is still off about 20% from its Aug 5. close, which we mostly chalk up to rising oil prices and interest rates. While elevated interest rates and commodity prices could weigh on shares in the near term, we believe the market can only overlook the positives for so long. articles.title: Đề xuất đầu tư 10.500 tỷ đồng vào 2 dự án du lịch nghỉ dưỡng, tiềm lực MBLand Đà Nẵng thế nào?
articles.text:
Đề xuất đầu tư 10.500 tỷ đồng vào 2 dự án du lịch nghỉ dưỡng, tiềm lực MBLand Đà Nẵng thế nào?
MBLand Đà Nẵng đề xuất đầu tư 2 dự án du lịch nghỉ dưỡng tại Đà Nẵng với tổng vốn dự kiến khoảng 10.500 tỷ đồng.
Cổng TTĐT TP.Đà Nẵng đăng tải, tại Hội nghị đối thoại giữa lãnh đạo thành phố với doanh nghiệp ngành du lịch năm 2026 mới đây, đại diện Công ty CP MBLand Đà Nẵng (MBLand Đà Nẵng) trình bày mong muốn tham gia nghiên cứu, đấu thầu các sản phẩm, dịch vụ du lịch chất lượng cao tại bãi biển Mỹ Khê, góp phần phát triển kinh tế đêm của TP.
Cụ thể, doanh nghiệp dự kiến đầu tư tổ hợp kinh tế đêm, nghỉ dưỡng, văn hóa và ẩm thực mang tên MBLand Mỹ Khê Paradise tại số 268 Võ Nguyên Giáp, phường Ngũ Hành Sơn. Khu đất có diện tích 11.465 m², nằm ở vị trí hai mặt tiền, đối diện bãi biển Mỹ Khê và khu phố du lịch An Thượng.
Tổ hợp có tổng mức đầu tư dự kiến 5.000 tỷ đồng, triển khai trong 3 giai đoạn. Các hạng mục chính gồm khu kinh tế đêm khoảng 8.000 m², khối khách sạn – văn phòng 10 tầng, quy mô 400 phòng và tuyến đường nội khu kết nối đường Trần Bạch Đằng với đường Võ Nguyên Giáp, mở lối đi từ khu phố An Thượng ra biển Mỹ Khê.
Theo tiến độ dự kiến của doanh nghiệp, khu kinh tế đêm sẽ khởi công vào tháng 11/2026, dự kiến đón khách từ tháng 4/2027. Khối khách sạn – văn phòng dự kiến khởi công ngày 30/4/2027.
Ngoài ra, MBLand Đà Nẵng cũng đề xuất phát triển Khu đô thị Đồng Nà – Bến Trễ, phường Hội An Tây, thành khu nghỉ dưỡng cao cấp mang tên MBLand Retreat sau khi hoàn tất các thủ tục liên quan. Tổng mức đầu tư dự kiến của dự án là 5.500 tỷ đồng.
Về MBLand Đà Nẵng, doanh nghiệp này được thành lập vào tháng 4/2016; trụ sở chính tại Tầng 6 Tòa nhà Bạch Đằng Complex số 50 Bạch Đằng, phường Hải Châu, TP.Đà Nẵng.
Vốn điều lệ của doanh nghiệp tính đến tháng 3/2022 ở mức 550 tỷ đồng, 100% là nguồn vốn tư nhân trong nước.
Hiện, MBLand Đà Nẵng do 3 thể nhân đứng tên gồm: Phó Chủ tịch HĐQT Phạm Tiên Tiến, Chủ tịch HĐQT Vũ Thành Huế và Tổng Giám đốc Lê Duẩn.
Bà Mai Thị Anh Đào (SN 1991) từng có thời gian đảm nhiệm vị trí Tổng Giám đốc, Người đại diện theo pháp luật của MBLand Đà Nẵng.
Bà Anh Đào còn được biết đến là người đại diện pháp luật của Công ty CP MBLand Tonkin Hội An (MBLand Tonkin Hội An).
Ba cổ đông sáng lập của MBLand Tonkin Hội An có mối quan hệ mật thiết với nhau khi Tasmania & Partner và Đông Phú 1932 là cổ đông sáng lập của Utopia Gaz.
Tháng 2/2022, Tasmania & Partner tiến hành sáp nhập doanh nghiệp với Đông Phú 1932.
MBLand Tonkin Hội An được thành lập vào tháng 5/2018 với vốn điều lệ 200 tỷ đồng; gồm 3 cổ đông sáng lập: Công ty CP Tập đoàn Tasmania & Partner 51%; Công ty CP Utopia Gaz 29% và Công ty TNHH Một thành viên Đông Phú 1932 20%.
Thời điểm này, ông Vũ Việt Dũng (SN 1978) là Chủ tịch HĐQT, Người đại diện theo pháp luật của MBLand Tonkin Hội An.
Đáng chú ý, ông Lê Duẩn cũng từng đảm nhiệm chức vụ Tổng Giám đốc, đại diện pháp luật MBLand Tonkin Hội An, sau đó chuyển giao vị trí này cho bà Mai Thị Anh Đào vào tháng 7/2023.
MBLand Đà Nẵng thuộc Tập đoàn MBLand Asset Management, hiện diện đầu tư tại Đà Nẵng và khu vực Quảng Nam (cũ) từ năm 2010.

articles.title: Có được dùng tiền gửi tiết kiệm làm tài sản bảo đảm để vay ngân hàng?
articles.text:
Có được dùng tiền gửi tiết kiệm làm tài sản bảo đảm để vay ngân hàng?
Bạn đọc Mạnh Khương (Lào Cai) hỏi: “Tôi có một khoản tiền gửi tiết kiệm tại ngân hàng nhưng chưa đến ngày đáo hạn. Hiện tôi đang cần tiền để giải quyết công việc cá nhân. Vậy tôi có thể dùng khoản tiết kiệm này làm tài sản bảo đảm để vay ngân hàng mà không phải rút tiền trước hạn không?”
Thời báo Ngân hàng xin cảm ơn bạn đã gửi câu hỏi. Sau đây là phần tư vấn:
Khi có nhu cầu vay vốn nhưng chưa muốn tất toán khoản tiết kiệm trước hạn, người gửi tiền có thể sử dụng chính khoản tiền tiết kiệm đó làm tài sản bảo đảm cho khoản vay tại ngân hàng. Tuy nhiên, việc cho vay còn phụ thuộc vào điều kiện và quy định của từng ngân hàng.
Theo quy định tại Điều 13 Thông tư số 48/2018/TT-NHNN của Ngân hàng Nhà nước về tiền gửi tiết kiệm, tiền gửi tiết kiệm được sử dụng làm tài sản bảo đảm theo hướng dẫn của tổ chức tín dụng, phù hợp với quy định pháp luật về giao dịch bảo đảm.
Như vậy, khách hàng có thể sử dụng khoản tiền gửi tiết kiệm để bảo đảm cho nghĩa vụ trả nợ tại ngân hàng mà không nhất thiết phải tất toán trước hạn. Đây là một phương án giúp người gửi tiền giải quyết nhu cầu vốn trong ngắn hạn, đồng thời có thể tiếp tục hưởng lãi từ khoản tiết kiệm theo thỏa thuận với ngân hàng.
Tuy nhiên, không phải cứ có sổ tiết kiệm là khách hàng đương nhiên được vay vốn. Ngân hàng sẽ xem xét nhu cầu vay, khả năng trả nợ, giá trị khoản tiền gửi và các điều kiện cấp tín dụng theo quy định. Hạn mức cho vay, lãi suất và thời hạn vay có thể khác nhau tùy từng ngân hàng.
Đáng chú ý, trong thời gian khoản tiết kiệm được sử dụng làm tài sản bảo đảm, khách hàng có thể bị hạn chế quyền rút tiền hoặc tất toán khoản tiền gửi theo thỏa thuận. Trường hợp không thực hiện đúng nghĩa vụ trả nợ, ngân hàng có quyền xử lý tài sản bảo đảm theo thỏa thuận và quy định pháp luật.
Vì vậy, trước khi quyết định vay, khách hàng nên tìm hiểu kỹ điều kiện vay vốn, lãi suất và thời hạn trả nợ. Đồng thời, cần cân nhắc chênh lệch giữa lãi suất vay và lãi suất tiết kiệm để tránh phát sinh chi phí không cần thiết.

articles.title: Anthropic is AI trade's last big hope for a major IPO this year
articles.text:
Heading into 2026, investors were excited at the prospect of a host of new initial public offerings, including ones from mega-cap private companies like SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI.
But now investors will have to settle for less than they expected at the start of the year, with OpenAI ruling out its debut on the public markets in 2026 and several other planned offerings postponed this year.
On prediction market platform Kalshi, speculators think the only major company left that might officially announce an IPO this year is Anthropic, which confidentially filed a prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission in early June.
The market on Kalshi asks traders if they think a series of companies will officially announce an IPO in 2026. The question of what constitutes an official announcement is resolved by the SEC declaring a company's S-1 effective, an IPO pricing or an exchange assigning a ticker to the stock. Contracts are resolved using various news outlets as sources.
Of the 23 companies that Kalshi lists on its market that remain open to trade, only Anthropic offers greater than 50% odds — 75% as of Monday morning — to officially announce an IPO this year.
Traders in January gave financial technology company Plaid 50% odds to debut on the public markets this year. They now place just a 10% chance the company, reportedly valued at $8 billion in the private market, goes public.
Human resources and payroll platform Deel had 50-50 odds as recently as February, but now speculators see only a 3% chance the company goes public in 2026. Cloud and artificial intelligence platform Databricks' odds are just 1%, after seeing more than 50% odds in January.
Similarly, OpenAI — Anthropic's chief rival — has just a 3% chance of going public after CEO Sam Altman said last month it didn't make sense to go public amid concerns over AI safety. Traders on Kalshi carry just 50-50 odds OpenAI makes an official IPO announcement by June 2027.
Growing postponements
IPO postponements, from across sectors, have grown in recent weeks. And while IPO proceeds this year are up sharply, driven by mega-cap debuts, notably SpaceX in June, the number of U.S. IPOs priced this year is actually down 33% compared with 2025, according to Renaissance Capital.
Investors are betting on major AI companies, as well as those whose products are contributing to the AI build-out, to move from private to public markets as they seek larger pools of capital to finance development. Many have grown at a blistering pace, and public markets are seen as the next step to support that growth.
Optimistic growth assumptions were called into question last week, however, when Anthropic revealed its revenue totaled $16.8 billion in the third quarter, weaker quarter-over-quarter growth than in past periods.
"More questions than answers emerged around the reasons for revenue growth deceleration in September and whether Anthropic can grow revenue at the rate the market is expecting given dynamics such as [large language model] pricing pressure," wrote 22V Research analyst Dauvin Peterson on Sunday. "At the end of the day, the revised IPO valuation range starting at $1.5T vs the prior expectation of at least $2T was viewed as disappointing and added fuel to the fire for the AI-related equities that were already under pressure."
Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

articles.title: Hà Nội rà soát thí điểm tổ hợp vui chơi, giải trí 24/7: Cú hích cho 'kinh tế đêm'
articles.text:
Hà Nội rà soát thí điểm tổ hợp vui chơi, giải trí 24/7: Cú hích cho 'kinh tế đêm'
Để hiện thực hóa mục tiêu đón hơn 50 triệu lượt khách vào năm 2030, Hà Nội sẽ rà soát và thí điểm các mô hình du lịch - thương mại hoạt động xuyên đêm (24/7). Cùng với việc mở thêm 3-5 tuyến phố đi bộ, Thủ đô đang từng bước lột xác để trở thành trung tâm giải trí không ngủ của khu vực.
Ngày 19/10/2026, Chủ tịch UBND Thành phố Hà Nội Vũ Đại Thắng ban hành kế hoạch về triển khai Chương trình hành động phát triển du lịch Việt Nam trở thành ngành kinh tế mũi nhọn trong kỷ nguyên mới, giai đoạn 2026 - 2030.
Mục tiêu chung của Kế hoạch hướng tới xây dựng Thủ đô Hà Nội trở thành trung tâm du lịch hàng đầu của cả nước, hạt nhân dẫn dắt, điều phối liên kết phát triển du lịch vùng, một trong ba cực tăng trưởng du lịch quốc gia; trung tâm du lịch văn hóa - di sản, sáng tạo, sự kiện và dịch vụ du lịch chất lượng cao của khu vực và quốc tế...
Hà Nội phấn đấu đến năm 2030, đón và phục vụ từ 47 - 50,5 triệu lượt khách du lịch; tổng thu từ khách du lịch đạt khoảng 295 - 340 nghìn tỷ đồng; quy mô phòng lưu trú du lịch tăng thêm tối thiểu 10.000 phòng cao cấp (hạng từ 4 - 5 sao); 3 khu du lịch được công nhận khu du lịch Quốc gia (khu du lịch hồ Hoàn Kiếm - phụ cận và khu phố cổ Hà Nội; khu du lịch Ba Vì; khu di tích quốc gia đặc biệt và thắng cảnh Hương Sơn) và các khu du lịch khác có đủ điều kiện.
Đồng thời hình thành được ít nhất 3 làng nghề, làng cổ là điểm đến du lịch chất lượng cao, có khả năng cạnh tranh trong khu vực, quốc tế và khả năng đáp ứng các tiêu chí, danh hiệu, giải thưởng quốc tế phù hợp (Làng cổ ở Đường Lâm - Sơn Tây đạt danh hiệu làng du lịch tốt nhất thế giới, làng nghề dệt lụa Vạn Phúc - Hà Đông, làng nghề gốm sứ Bát Tràng đạt danh hiệu quốc tế về du lịch làng nghề)...
Mô hình du lịch - giải trí - thương mại hoạt động 24/7
Về phát triển kinh tế ban đêm, Hà Nội sẽ rà soát, lựa chọn các khu vực có đủ điều kiện, xây dựng phương án thí điểm mô hình du lịch - giải trí - thương mại hoạt động 24/7. Lựa chọn các trung tâm thương mại, trung tâm du lịch, điểm mua sắm có tỷ trọng khách quốc tế cao, đủ điều kiện để triển khai cơ chế hoàn thuế giá trị gia tăng; phối hợp với các cơ quan Trung ương và đơn vị liên quan chuẩn bị các điều kiện cần thiết để triển khai theo quy định hiện hành.
Hoàn thiện đầu tư các điều kiện để được công nhận 3 khu du lịch quốc gia (Ba Vì; khu di tích quốc gia đặc biệt và thắng cảnh Hương Sơn; khu vực hồ Hoàn Kiếm - phụ cận và khu phố cổ Hà Nội). Hoàn thành lập, triển khai đồ án Quy hoạch chi tiết tỷ lệ 1/500 và Đề án bảo tồn, phát triển làng nghề, làng cổ, không gian văn hóa kết hợp du lịch đối với một số làng nghề: dệt lụa Vạn Phúc, gốm sứ Bát Tràng, khảm trai, sơn mài Chuyên Mỹ, làng cổ ở Đường Lâm, không gian văn hóa - lịch sử địa phương Minh Châu,… trên địa bàn các xã, phường trọng điểm thành điểm du lịch đạt tiêu chuẩn quốc tế...
Phát triển sản phẩm công nghiệp văn hóa thương hiệu Thủ đô, quốc gia, quốc tế phù hợp với từng phân khúc thị trường khách trên địa bàn các phường: Hoàn Kiếm, Cửa Nam. Hình thành và phát triển các Trung tâm công nghiệp văn hóa. Hình thành và phát triển mới: 3 - 5 tuyến phố đi bộ gắn với tuyến phố ẩm thực, biểu diễn văn hóa theo chủ đề, du lịch đêm; 3 - 5 mô hình du lịch nông nghiệp, nông thôn; 2 - 3 tổ hợp du lịch thể thao chuyên nghiệp.
Phát triển không gian văn hóa, du lịch, vui chơi giải trí quanh hồ Hoàn Kiếm, hồ Tây; thu hút khoảng 5 triệu lượt khách hằng năm. Xây dựng và phát triển hệ sinh thái sản phẩm du lịch “Hà Nội 12 tháng - 12 sắc màu trải nghiệm” và thương hiệu “Thu Hà Nội”...
Tiền phong

articles.title: Healthcare is catching the rotation out of AI. Josh Brown's list includes two names that can benefit
articles.text: (This is The Best Stocks in the Market , brought to you by Josh Brown and Sean Russo of Ritholtz Wealth Management.) Josh — Money doesn't leave the market. It moves, and the list is where we see it first. The Best Stocks in the Market list is built by the market, and this week the market is saying healthcare. My friend Adam Parker at Trivariate Research put out a note on Thursday asking what everyone means when they say they like the sector. Adam has been recommending healthcare for 21 months. By his own account, the call went from early to wrong to decent, and now some of his clients are calling it crowded. He doesn't buy that. He argues the appeal comes from fast growth and upward estimate revisions, and he gives little weight to how cheap the sector looks against its own history. Adam also finds that parts of healthcare have low correlation to the companies riding AI revenue, which gives investors a different set of drivers. One of the fast-growth themes he singles out is life science and bioprocess tools, and it has beaten the rest of the sector this year. That's the neighborhood two of today's names live in. Waters (WAT) makes the instruments labs use to separate and identify molecules, and it's new to this column. Thermo Fisher Scientific (TMO) is the largest company in life science tools. We nailed the call the last time we wrote about TMO last fall , so an update is long overdue. Sean's got the usual Monday morning highlights from the list. I'll be back with some technical commentary and risk management. As of Oct 19, there are 140 names on The Best Stocks in the Market list. Top sector ranking: Top industries: Top 5 best stocks by relative strength: Spotlight: Healthcare Sean — Healthcare is catching the rotation out of AI. Wednesday's hotter-than-expected CPI print sent tech down 3% on the day, while healthcare was the best-performing S & P 500 sector, up 2.4%. It led again Thursday, up 1.8%. XLV gained 5.4% over the five sessions ended Oct. 15. To be clear, it's not the only sector working. Through Oct. 14, energy (+51%) and tech (+32%) are the only sectors ahead of the S & P 500 this year. But healthcare is now third at +12.4%, within a point of the index (+12.9%) after a stretch of mid returns. The sector entered 2026 with its forward P/E relative to the market in the lowest quintile of its 15-year range. With this set up, we wanted to take a look at some charts within the sector. A pulse check on healthcare! Waters Corp. (WAT): Waters makes the instruments and consumables used to separate and identify molecules and the software that runs on its instruments. Its customers are mostly pharma and biotech, along with academic labs and food and environmental companies. In February, Waters closed a combination with BD's Biosciences & Diagnostic Solutions business, which roughly doubled its revenue base. We haven't written about WAT before. The stock fell 9% to 12% when the BD deal was announced in July 2025, then bottomed at $283 in mid-March, down 24.6% for 2026 at that point. It's up 57% from that low to $444, about 2% below its record high of $454.54 set Oct. 6. Waters reported Q2 earnings on Aug. 4th with revenue of $1.65 billion and adjusted EPS of $3.05, both topping expectations. The legacy WAT business did $828M, up 9% and the new BD unit did $817 million, up 4% in its first full quarter. Management raised full-year organic constant-currency growth to 7%-9% and adjusted EPS to $14.45-$14.65 (+10-12%). WAT guided Q3 to $1.75 billion-$1.762 billion in revenue and $3.95-$4.05 in EPS. WAT trades at about 30x the midpoint of 2026 EPS guidance and reports again on Nov. 3. Risk management: Josh — Waters ripped out of a spring base in late May, and the Aug. 4th earnings report Sean described above lifted it again. The stock ran roughly $40 in a single session on about double its usual volume. Dips since have found buyers near $390. A September breakout carried it to a record near $455 on Oct. 6, and it has chopped between $422 and $450 since. Friday's close was $437, with the 50-day rising at $421 and the 200-day at $366. The $455 high is the level to clear. With RSI at 56, momentum is sitting in the middle of its range after a full lap. It ran up to 70 at the end of September on the way to the record, cooled to the mid-40s by Oct. 2, and has bounced between there and the low 60s while price stayed within a few percent of the high. That's a base for another try at the record. Traders can use $420 as a good enough stop. I'd use closing prices. Those are the early October lows, and the rising 50-day at $421 lands in the same spot. That's not an accident. A close below it and the range has broken to the downside. It's a tight leash, and that's the point. Investors can anchor to $390. The August 6th low and the September low both came in right there, two tests of the same spot, with the 200-day at $366 sitting well underneath. A weekly close below $390 and the uptrend has failed. Thermo Fisher Scientific, Inc. (TMO): Sean — Thermo Fisher is the largest company in life science tools, with about $46 billion in trailing revenue. It sells analytical instruments, lab consumables, diagnostics and bioproduction equipment. It also runs the pharma services and clinical research business that drug developers outsource trials to. Pharma and biotech are about 60% of revenue. We last mentioned TMO on Nov. 24, when Josh showed the chart pressing against its highs at a $220 billion market cap and said, "gun to my head, it's gonna go." It went! The stock is up 19% since then and closed Thursday at a record $696.49, a $257.5B market cap. That's 60% above its 52-week low of $435.27, 20.5% year to date and 31% since mid-July, right before it reported Q2 earnings. Five analysts raised price targets in the last two weeks, with JPMorgan and TD Cowen both at $760. Guggenheim initiated at buy with a $740 target on Thursday. TMO reported its Q2 report in July with revenue of $11.99 billion (+10%, 5% organic) and adjusted EPS of $6.03 (+13%), and adjusted operating margin up 0.9 points to 22.8%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $47.4 billion-$48.1 billion and adjusted EPS to $24.93-$25.33 (+9%-11%). It guided free cash flow to $6.9 billion-$7.4 billion and a planned $4 billion in buybacks. The company has also closed the Clario and Solventum filtration acquisitions, and sold its microbiology business for $1.075B in August. At a September conference, management said orders are running ahead of revenue, and the stock rose 4.6% that day. There is a lot of momentum in this name from management, analysts, and price. TMO trades at about 25.6x forward earnings and reports Q3 this Wednesday, Oct. 21, before the open. Consensus is $6.40 in EPS on $11.91 billion in revenue. Risk management: Josh — Thermo Fisher gapped out of a long base on July 23, opening near $570 after closing in the $520s the day before. The Q2 report Sean described above is the reason. That's a breakaway gap, and it has stayed open for three months. The stock hasn't been back below $555 since. It ran to $645 by late August, pulled back to $597 in early September, and reached a high near $693 on Oct. 6 that reversed hard. After a week of digestion it took that high out on Thursday and printed a record near $703. Friday's close was $690, with the 50-day rising at $637 and the 200-day at $547. Thursday's high is the level to clear. RSI is 64. It ran up to 70 in late September, washed out to the mid-40s on the early October pullback, and is back at 64 with the stock at a record. The stock gave back about 7% to do it. Momentum is fully rested and the price is already at new highs. Traders can use $650 as their stop. That's the bottom of the late September and early October range, where the stock kept finding buyers before this week's breakout. A close below it puts the stock back inside the box and says the breakout didn't take. The chart will let you know in short order, and with the Q3 report due Wednesday morning, it may not take long. Judge it on the close, not the intraday swings. Investors can anchor to $600, the early September low and the base of the run since the August high. The gap sits far below that, and the 200-day is too distant to act on. A weekly close below $600 and the uptrend that began with the July gap has lost its footing. The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note edged up to 5.13% on Monday, following a nearly 15bps decline the previous week, as traders continued to weigh domestic inflation and interest rate expectations against broader geopolitical developments. Investors are currently pricing in an nearly 83% probability that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate unchanged next week, while the odds of a 25bps rate hike in December stand at around 75%. Speaking at the IMF’s annual meetings in Bangkok on Friday, Fed Chair Warsh refrained from signaling the outcome of this month’s FOMC meeting, noting that hotter-than-expected inflation had not altered his assessment of the US economy. His remarks helped reinforce market expectations that the Fed would hold rates steady. Both CPI and PPI reports released last week came in hotter than expected. articles.title: Xuất khẩu cà phê lập kỷ lục, mang về 8,5 tỷ USD
articles.text:
Xuất khẩu cà phê lập kỷ lục, mang về 8,5 tỷ USD
Kết thúc niên vụ 2025-2026, Việt Nam đã xuất khẩu 1,8 triệu tấn cà phê, mang về 8,5 tỷ USD cao nhất từ trước đến nay dù giá thế giới điều chỉnh giảm.
- 20-10-2026Qatar lại báo tin vui đến cả thế giới
- 19-10-2026Việt Nam có một tỷ phú sang Lào, Campuchia trồng bưởi nuôi bò: Sản lượng 60.000 tấn trái mỗi vụ, mục tiêu sở hữu hơn 200.000 con bò
- 19-10-2026Việt Nam có một tỷ phú sang Campuchia trồng hơn 2.000 ha dứa: Được tập đoàn Mỹ 135 năm tuổi bắt tay hợp tác, sản lượng dự kiến 100.000 tấn/năm
Số liệu vừa được Hiệp hội Cà phê - Ca cao Việt Nam (VICOFA) công bố hôm nay, 19/10 tại Hội nghị tổng kết niên vụ cà phê 2025-2026, triển khai phương hướng nhiệm vụ niên vụ 2026-2027 tổ chức tại TP Hồ Chí Minh.
Theo VICOFA, so với niên vụ 2024-2025, sản lượng cà phê xuất khẩu tăng 21% nhưng kim ngạch không tăng tương ứng, chỉ 1%. Nguyên nhân là nguồn cung thế giới phục hồi khiến thị trường bắt đầu chịu sức ép điều chỉnh. Giá xuất khẩu bình quân của cà phê Robusta, mặt hàng chủ lực của Việt Nam đạt quanh mức 3.500- 4.000 USD/tấn.
Trong 1,8 triệu tấn cà phê xuất khẩu, cà phê nhân xanh đạt 1,65 triệu tấn với 7 tỷ USD. Khối lượng xuất khẩu tăng 21,4% nhưng kim ngạch giảm 1,5% so với niên vụ trước.
Niên vụ 2024-2025, Việt Nam xuất khẩu trên 1,5 triệu tấn cà phê mang về hơn 8,4 tỷ USD. Giá xuất khẩu bình quân đạt 5.610 USD/tấn - mức cao chưa từng có trong lịch sử ngành cà phê Việt Nam.
Theo VICOFA, trong niên vụ này, có 4 doanh nghiệp xuất khẩu cà phê nhân xanh vượt trên 100.000 tấn. Trong đó, Công ty TNHH Vĩnh Hiệp tiếp tục giữ vị trí số 1 với gần 180.000 tấn, chiếm 10% kim ngạch toàn ngành và mang về hơn 836 triệu USD.
VICOFA đánh giá, một trong những điểm sáng của niên vụ 2025-2026 là sự chuyển dịch từ xuất khẩu cà phê nhân xanh sang cà phê hòa tan, cà phê tinh chế, cà phê phối trộn diễn ra mạnh mẽ với hàng loạt nhà máy công nghệ cao.
Theo đó, cà phê chế biến sâu xuất khẩu đạt khoảng 142.600 tấn, thu về 1,5 tỷ USD. So với niên vụ trước, khối lượng tăng khoảng 15%, còn giá trị tăng 14%. Đặc biệt, doanh nghiệp xuất khẩu cà phê Việt Nam đang quyết tâm đẩy mạnh đầu tư vào chế biến sâu, giảm dần tỷ lệ xuất khẩu cà phê nhân.
Cả niên vụ 2025-2026, Việt Nam sản xuất sản lượng cà phê Việt Nam gần 1,9 triệu tấn, tăng khoảng 10% so với niên vụ 2024-2025. Trong đó, Robusta chiếm 90% sản lượng. Theo tổ chức Cà phê Quốc tế (IOC), Việt Nam xếp thứ hai thế giới sau Brazil về sản lượng cà phê nhưng dẫn đầu toàn cầu về cà phê Robusta.
